<!-- https://playx-flutter.github.io/playx_core/getting-started/ -->
# Getting started

## Requirements

| | Minimum |
| --- | --- |
| Dart | 3.12 |
| Flutter | 3.44 |

Supported platforms: Android, iOS, macOS, Windows, Linux and web.

## Installation

```yaml
dependencies:
  playx_core: ^2.0.0
```

Using the full PlayX ecosystem? Depend on [`playx`](https://pub.dev/packages/playx) instead, which includes `playx_core`.

```dart
import 'package:playx_core/playx_core.dart';
```

One import gives you everything: preferences, secure storage, environment configuration, extensions, utilities, logging, and re-exports of `GetIt`, `Equatable`, `SharedPreferences` and `worker_manager`.

## Booting the core

Call `PlayxCore.bootCore` once, before `runApp`. It creates the pieces you ask for and initializes logging and dependency injection.

```dart
Future<void> main() async {
  WidgetsFlutterBinding.ensureInitialized();

  await PlayxCore.bootCore();

  runApp(const MyApp());
}
```

With no arguments it creates `PlayxPrefs`, `PlayxAsyncPrefs`, `PlayxSecurePrefs` (using `flutter_secure_storage`) and the worker manager. Everything is configured through settings objects:

```dart
await PlayxCore.bootCore(
  // Which preference stores to create.
  prefsSettings: const PlayxPrefsSettings(
    createPlayxPrefsWithCache: true,
  ),
  // Secure storage backend and behavior.
  securePrefsSettings: const PlayxSecurePrefsSettings(
    storageType: PlayxSecureStorageType.auto,
  ),
  // Environment configuration. Omit to skip loading any env.
  envSettings: const PlayxEnvSettings(
    requiredKeys: ['API_URL'],
  ),
  // Isolate pool used by the *InIsolate helpers.
  workerManagerSettings: const WorkManagerSettings(isolatesCount: 2),
  // How the package's own logs look: no colors, with the time, no box.
  loggerSettings: PlayxLoggerSettings(
    useColors: false,
    printDateTime: true,
    formatter: const DefaultColoredLoggerFormatter(),
  ),
);
```

### What `bootCore` sets up

`bootCore` runs these steps in order. Each is skipped when its setting turns it off.

| Step | Setting | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Create `PlayxPrefs` | `prefsSettings.createPlayxPrefs` | `true` |
| Create `PlayxAsyncPrefs` | `prefsSettings.createPlayxAsyncPrefs` | `true` |
| Create `PlayxPrefsWithCache` | `prefsSettings.createPlayxPrefsWithCache` (with `prefsWithCacheOptions`) | `false` |
| Create `PlayxSecurePrefs` | `securePrefsSettings.createSecurePrefs` | `true` |
| Load `PlayxEnv` | `envSettings` is not `null` | not loaded |
| Start the worker manager | `workerManagerSettings.initWorkerManager` (with `isolatesCount`, `dynamicSpawning`) | `true` |

The logger named `PLAYX CORE` is always initialized first (configure it with `loggerSettings`), and `GetIt` becomes available at the end.

`bootCore` throws if loading the env fails (for example a missing `requiredKeys` entry, or `isOptional: false` with a missing file), so a misconfigured build fails at startup rather than deep inside the app.

> Create only what you use. Skipping a store you don't need avoids reading it at startup, and calling a store that wasn't created throws an `Exception` saying so.

## Dependency injection

`playx_core` re-exports [`GetIt`](https://pub.dev/packages/get_it). After `bootCore`, use the global `getIt`:

```dart
getIt.registerSingleton<AuthService>(AuthService());
getIt.registerLazySingleton<Api>(() => Api(PlayxEnv.getUri('API_URL', fallback: Uri())));

final auth = getIt<AuthService>();
```

`getIt` (and `PlayxCore.getIt`) throws an `Exception` if `bootCore` hasn't run. `PlayxCore.dispose()` resets it.

## Logging

`bootCore` creates the logger `PLAYX CORE`, used by the package itself (for example when a secure storage fallback happens). You can use it too, or create your own. Pass `loggerSettings` to turn colors off, add the time, hide the boot messages or change where logs go: see [Logging](logging.md#configuring-the-playx-core-logger).

```dart
PlayxCore.logger.i('App started');
```

## Disposing

`PlayxCore.dispose()` releases everything `bootCore` created: `GetIt`, the preference stores, `PlayxSecurePrefs`, `PlayxEnv` and the worker manager. It is mainly useful in tests:

```dart
tearDown(PlayxCore.dispose);
```

See [Testing](testing.md) for complete test setups.

## What next

- Store data: [Preferences](preferences.md) and [Secure preferences](secure-prefs.md).
- Configure the app per environment: [Environment configuration](env.md), and [Secure env](secure-env.md) for sensitive values.
- Upgrading from 1.x? Read [Migrating to 2.0](migration-2.0.md).

---

<!-- https://playx-flutter.github.io/playx_core/preferences/ -->
# Preferences

`playx_core` wraps the [`shared_preferences`](https://pub.dev/packages/shared_preferences) plugin in three static helpers with the same typed API. They store plain (unencrypted) values; for secrets use [secure preferences](secure-prefs.md).

## Which one should I use?

| | `PlayxPrefs` | `PlayxAsyncPrefs` | `PlayxPrefsWithCache` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Backed by | `SharedPreferences` | `SharedPreferencesAsync` | `SharedPreferencesWithCache` |
| Reads | synchronous | `Future` | synchronous (from a cache) |
| Writes | `Future<void>` | `Future<void>` | `Future<void>` |
| Always reads the latest platform value | no (in-memory snapshot) | **yes** | no, until `reloadCache()` |
| Created at boot | by default | by default | opt-in (`createPlayxPrefsWithCache`) |

- **`PlayxPrefs`** is the simplest choice: read values synchronously in `build` methods or `initState`.
- **`PlayxAsyncPrefs`** always asks the platform, so it is the right choice when other isolates, processes or native code may change the same preferences.
- **`PlayxPrefsWithCache`** reads synchronously from a cache that can be limited to an allow list, and refreshed with `reloadCache()`.

> The three stores are independent: a value saved with one is not guaranteed to be visible to the others. Pick one per kind of data.

## Setting up

`bootCore` creates them according to `PlayxPrefsSettings`:

```dart
await PlayxCore.bootCore(
  prefsSettings: const PlayxPrefsSettings(
    createPlayxPrefs: true,            // default
    createPlayxAsyncPrefs: true,       // default
    createPlayxPrefsWithCache: true,   // default: false
    prefsWithCacheOptions: SharedPreferencesWithCacheOptions(
      allowList: {'theme', 'locale'},  // optional: only cache these keys
    ),
  ),
);
```

Or create one yourself: `await PlayxPrefs.create();`.

Using a store that hasn't been created is safe for reads (they return `null` or the fallback) and throws an `Exception` for the `sharedPrefs` getter.

## Reading and writing

All three classes offer the same methods. `PlayxPrefs` and `PlayxPrefsWithCache` return values directly; `PlayxAsyncPrefs` returns `Future`s.

| Type | Read (`null` if missing) | Read with fallback (default) | Write |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `String` | `maybeGetString(key)` | `getString(key, fallback: '')` | `setString(key, value)` |
| `int` | `maybeGetInt(key)` | `getInt(key, fallback: -1)` | `setInt(key, value)` |
| `double` | `maybeGetDouble(key)` | `getDouble(key, fallback: -1)` | `setDouble(key, value)` |
| `bool` | `maybeGetBool(key)` | `getBool(key, fallback: false)` | `setBool(key, value)` |

```dart
// PlayxPrefs: synchronous reads.
await PlayxPrefs.setString('name', 'John Doe');
await PlayxPrefs.setInt('age', 25);

final name = PlayxPrefs.getString('name');                 // 'John Doe'
final age = PlayxPrefs.getInt('age');                      // 25
final height = PlayxPrefs.maybeGetDouble('height');        // null
final darkMode = PlayxPrefs.getBool('dark', fallback: true);

// PlayxAsyncPrefs: awaited reads.
await PlayxAsyncPrefs.setString('token', 'abc');
final token = await PlayxAsyncPrefs.getString('token');
```

Reads never throw: a missing key, a value of another type, or a store that isn't initialized all give `null` (`maybeGet*`) or the fallback (`get*`).

### Other operations

```dart
PlayxPrefs.find('name');            // the raw value (Object?), or null
await PlayxPrefs.remove('name');    // delete one key
await PlayxPrefs.clear();           // delete everything in this store
await PlayxPrefs.dispose();         // forget the instance (mostly for tests)

await PlayxPrefsWithCache.reloadCache();   // refresh the cache from the platform
```

On `PlayxAsyncPrefs`, `find` returns a `Future<Object?>`.

## Maps, lists and objects

Every preference class (including [`PlayxSecurePrefs`](secure-prefs.md)) can store structured data. Values are saved as JSON strings.

| | Read (`null` if unusable) | Read with fallback | Write |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Map | `maybeGetMap(key)` | `getMap(key, fallback: {})` | `setMap(key, map)` |
| List | `maybeGetList<T>(key, fromJson:)` | `getList<T>(key, fallback: [], fromJson:)` | `setList<T>(key, list, toJson:)` |
| Object | `maybeGetObject<T>(key, fromJson:)` | `getObject<T>(key, fromJson:, fallback:)` | `setObject<T>(key, value, toJson:)` |

```dart
// Maps
await PlayxPrefs.setMap('settings', {'theme': 'dark', 'fontSize': 14});
final settings = PlayxPrefs.getMap('settings');            // Map<String, dynamic>

// Lists of JSON values need no converters...
await PlayxPrefs.setList('ids', [1, 2, 3]);
final ids = PlayxPrefs.getList<int>('ids');                // [1, 2, 3]

// ...lists of your own types do.
await PlayxAsyncPrefs.setList('users', users, toJson: (u) => u.toJson());
final saved = await PlayxAsyncPrefs.getList(
  'users',
  fromJson: User.fromJson,
);

// Single objects
await PlayxSecurePrefs.setObject('user', user, toJson: (u) => u.toJson());
final user = await PlayxSecurePrefs.maybeGetObject(
  'user',
  fromJson: User.fromJson,
);
```

`fromJson` receives the decoded JSON (`dynamic`), so the [safe JSON helpers](utilities.md#safe-json-access) work well there:

```dart
class User {
  final String name;
  final int age;
  const User(this.name, this.age);

  factory User.fromJson(dynamic json) =>
      User(asString(json, 'name'), asIntOr(json, 'age'));

  Map<String, dynamic> toJson() => {'name': name, 'age': age};
}
```

**What happens with bad data**

- `maybeGet*` returns `null` and `get*` returns its fallback when the key is missing, the stored string isn't valid JSON, has another shape (for example a list where a map is expected), an item can't be converted, or `fromJson` throws.
- `setMap` and `setList` without `toJson` accept JSON values and objects with a `toJson()` method. Anything else (for example a `DateTime`) throws a `JsonUnsupportedObjectError`, so convert it first.

## Tips

- Prefer a few well-named keys; consider a constants class (`abstract class PrefKeys { static const theme = 'theme'; }`).
- Store small settings, not large documents or binary data.
- Writes return a `Future`; `await` them when the next read depends on the write (for `PlayxPrefsWithCache` and `PlayxPrefs` the in-memory value updates immediately).
- To observe changes in a UI, keep the value in your state management and write through to preferences.

See also: [Testing](testing.md) for `setMockInitialValues`, [Secure preferences](secure-prefs.md) for encrypted storage.

---

<!-- https://playx-flutter.github.io/playx_core/secure-prefs/ -->
# Secure preferences

`PlayxSecurePrefs` stores small secrets (tokens, keys, credentials) encrypted at rest. It has the same typed API as the [other preference stores](preferences.md), but every operation is asynchronous, and you choose **where** the data lives.

- [Quick start](#quick-start)
- [Choosing a backend](#choosing-a-backend)
- [Settings reference](#settings-reference)
- [The `auto` backend](#the-auto-backend)
- [Encrypted preferences](#encrypted-preferences)
- [Hiding key names](#hiding-key-names-encryptkeys)
- [Web](#web)
- [Switching an existing app](#switching-an-existing-app-from-flutter_secure_storage)
- [Errors and failures](#errors-and-failures)
- [Security notes](#security-notes)

## Quick start

`PlayxCore.bootCore` creates it with the default settings:

```dart
await PlayxCore.bootCore();

await PlayxSecurePrefs.setString('access_token', 'abc123');
final token = await PlayxSecurePrefs.getString('access_token');
final missing = await PlayxSecurePrefs.maybeGetString('nope');   // null

await PlayxSecurePrefs.remove('access_token');
await PlayxSecurePrefs.clear();
```

Typed values and structured data work like the other stores:

```dart
await PlayxSecurePrefs.setInt('attempts', 3);
await PlayxSecurePrefs.setBool('biometrics', true);
await PlayxSecurePrefs.setDouble('balance', 12.5);
await PlayxSecurePrefs.setMap('session', {'id': 7, 'role': 'admin'});
await PlayxSecurePrefs.setObject('user', user, toJson: (u) => u.toJson());
```

| Type | Read (`null` if missing) | Read with fallback | Write |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `String` | `maybeGetString` | `getString` (`''`) | `setString` |
| `int` | `maybeGetInt` | `getInt` (`-1`) | `setInt` |
| `double` | `maybeGetDouble` | `getDouble` (`-1`) | `setDouble` |
| `bool` | `maybeGetBool` | `getBool` (`false`) | `setBool` |
| Map / List / Object | `maybeGetMap`, `maybeGetList`, `maybeGetObject` | `getMap`, `getList`, `getObject` | `setMap`, `setList`, `setObject` |

Numbers and bools are stored as strings and parsed back; a value that can't be parsed reads as `null` (so `getBool` returns its fallback). See [Preferences](preferences.md#maps-lists-and-objects) for maps, lists and objects.

Other members:

| Member | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `PlayxSecurePrefs.storageType` | The backend actually in use, e.g. after an `auto` fallback. |
| `PlayxSecurePrefs.isInitialized` | Whether `create` has been called. |
| `PlayxSecurePrefs.securePrefs` | The underlying `FlutterSecureStorage` instance (always created). |
| `PlayxSecurePrefs.create(securePrefsSettings:)` | Create it yourself instead of through `bootCore`. |
| `PlayxSecurePrefs.dispose()` | Release it (mostly for tests). |
| `PlayxSecurePrefs.migrateFromFlutterSecureStorage()` | Move data from `flutter_secure_storage`. See [below](#switching-an-existing-app-from-flutter_secure_storage). |

## Choosing a backend

Select it with `PlayxSecurePrefsSettings.storageType`. The API stays the same whichever you pick.

| `PlayxSecureStorageType` | Stores values in | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `flutterSecureStorage` (default) | [`flutter_secure_storage`](https://pub.dev/packages/flutter_secure_storage): Keystore-backed storage on Android, Keychain on iOS and macOS, DPAPI on Windows, libsecret on Linux | The default of previous versions. No startup health check. |
| `simpleSecureStorage` | [`simple_secure_storage`](https://pub.dev/packages/simple_secure_storage): the same native stores through a different, actively maintained plugin | Initialization errors are thrown (unless `throwOnError: false`). |
| `encryptedPrefs` | `SharedPreferencesAsync`, each value encrypted with AES-256-GCM | The key lives in a secure store, with a fallback. Works anywhere preferences work. |
| `auto` | The first healthy backend of `autoOrder` | **Recommended** when you want the app to keep working on devices where a plugin fails. |
| `memory` | A map in memory | Nothing survives a restart. For tests, or as a last resort. |

```dart
await PlayxCore.bootCore(
  securePrefsSettings: const PlayxSecurePrefsSettings(
    storageType: PlayxSecureStorageType.auto,
  ),
);
```

**Which should I pick?**

- *Existing app, no problems with `flutter_secure_storage`:* keep the default.
- *Seeing plugin errors or crashes on some devices:* use `auto` with `simple_secure_storage` first. Data in the old store can be moved with [`migrateFromFlutterSecureStorage`](#switching-an-existing-app-from-flutter_secure_storage).
- *Web:* nothing to choose; every type except `memory` uses [WebCrypto](#web).
- *Tests:* `memory`.

## Settings reference

### `PlayxSecurePrefsSettings`

| Option | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `storageType` | `flutterSecureStorage` | The backend. |
| `autoOrder` | `[simpleSecureStorage, flutterSecureStorage, encryptedPrefs]` | Order `auto` tries backends in. Only these three types are allowed; `memory` is always the last resort. The first entry is the *preferred* backend. |
| `throwOnError` | `true` | When `false`, errors are logged instead of thrown: reads return `null`, writes are ignored, and `memory` is used if the backend can't be created. |
| `encryptKeys` | `false` | Hide key names. See [below](#hiding-key-names-encryptkeys). |
| `flutterSecureStorageOptions` | defaults | Platform options for `flutter_secure_storage`. |
| `simpleSecureStorageOptions` | defaults | Options for `simple_secure_storage`. |
| `encryptedPrefsOptions` | defaults | Options for `encryptedPrefs`. |
| `clearOnReinstall` | `true` | Clear the store on the first start after a reinstall (the iOS and macOS Keychain survives uninstalling). |
| `createSecurePrefs` | `true` | Whether `bootCore` creates it. |

### `PlayxFlutterSecureStorageOptions`

Groups the native `flutter_secure_storage` options: `iosOptions`, `androidOptions`, `linuxOptions`, `windowsOptions`, `macOsOptions`. Defaults use `KeychainAccessibility.first_unlock` on iOS.

```dart
const PlayxSecurePrefsSettings(
  flutterSecureStorageOptions: PlayxFlutterSecureStorageOptions(
    iosOptions: IOSOptions(accessibility: KeychainAccessibility.unlocked),
  ),
);
```

### `PlayxSimpleSecureStorageOptions`

| Option | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `appName` | `null` | Your app name, used by the plugin on some platforms. |
| `namespace` | `null` | Your app namespace, e.g. `com.example.app`. |
| `prefix` | `'sss_'` | Prepended to every key to avoid conflicts. |
| `darwinAccessibility` | `afterFirstUnlock` | Keychain accessibility on iOS and macOS. |

### `PlayxEncryptedPrefsOptions`

| Option | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `keyPrefix` | `'playx_secure_'` | Prefix of every key stored in preferences. It isolates secure values from your other preferences, so `clear()` only removes keys with this prefix. Must not be empty. |
| `keyStores` | `[simpleSecureStorage, flutterSecureStorage]` | Where the encryption key is kept, in order of preference. Only these two are allowed. |

## The `auto` backend

`auto` picks a backend **at every start**:

1. For each type in `autoOrder`, it creates the backend and runs a **health check**: write a random value, read it back, delete it.
2. The first backend that passes is used. Failures are logged, not thrown.
3. If none passes, it uses `memory`, so the app still starts (nothing is persisted that session).

```dart
// Prefer simple_secure_storage, fall back to encrypted preferences.
const PlayxSecurePrefsSettings(
  storageType: PlayxSecureStorageType.auto,
  autoOrder: [
    PlayxSecureStorageType.simpleSecureStorage,
    PlayxSecureStorageType.encryptedPrefs,
  ],
);
```

### Data follows the preferred backend

If a fallback was used in one session, `auto` keeps a small journal (in preferences) of what happened, so the data can be moved to the preferred backend on a later start where it works again:

- values written during the fallback are moved back;
- values removed during the fallback stay removed;
- a `clear()` during the fallback (for example a logout) is applied to the preferred backend too;
- an older fallback value never overwrites a newer one.

The journal contains key names and backend names, never values. With `encryptKeys: true` it is encrypted as well.

> **Native crashes can't be caught.** Only Dart exceptions trigger a fallback. If a plugin crashes the app natively on some devices, put it last in `autoOrder` or remove it.

## Encrypted preferences

`encryptedPrefs` encrypts each value with **AES-256-GCM** (with a random nonce per value, and authentication, so tampering is detected) and saves it in `SharedPreferencesAsync`. Two keys are involved:

- **The primary key**: random bytes generated on the device, kept in the first healthy store of `keyStores` (on web, a [non-extractable WebCrypto key](#web)). A marker in preferences remembers which store holds it.
- **The fallback key**: random bytes kept in plain preferences, used when the primary key can't be loaded. It only **obfuscates** the data: anyone with the preferences file can decrypt it.

Each stored value records which key encrypted it, so values written with the fallback key stay readable once the primary key is back.

### Protecting the primary key

The key is never discarded while values encrypted with it may still be readable:

| Situation | What happens |
| --- | --- |
| The key store is unavailable this session | The fallback key is used; the stored key is left untouched. |
| The key store works but the key reads back missing or invalid | The fallback key is used; the stored key is **not** replaced. |
| It stays missing for **3 starts in a row** (for example the Android Keystore was reset) | The key is considered lost: values encrypted with it are removed (they can't be decrypted anymore) and a new key is created. |
| The key is missing and there is no data that needs it | A new key is created right away. |
| A key store is removed from `keyStores` later | An existing key is still read from where it was created; `keyStores` only decides where **new** keys go. |

## Hiding key names (`encryptKeys`)

Encrypting values doesn't hide **key names** such as `access_token`: some stores keep them readable in files. Enable `encryptKeys` to store each value under a keyed hash (HMAC-SHA256) of its name instead:

```dart
const PlayxSecurePrefsSettings(
  storageType: PlayxSecureStorageType.auto,
  encryptKeys: true,
);
```

| Storage | Names with `encryptKeys: true` |
| --- | --- |
| `encryptedPrefs` (every platform, so all of web) | Hidden; only `keyPrefix` stays visible |
| `flutterSecureStorage` on Android | Hidden (otherwise plain text in a private preferences file) |
| `simpleSecureStorage` on Android | Already encrypted by the plugin |
| iOS and macOS Keychain | Kept by the OS, out of app files |
| Windows and Linux credential stores | Not hidden |

How it works:

- The hash key is kept in secure storage (the keystore, or a non-extractable WebCrypto key on web), so names can't be guessed from the files alone.
- The real name is stored **inside** the encrypted value, so `readAll`, migrations and recovery keep working.
- It can be turned on or off at any time: stored values are converted on the next start. For `flutter_secure_storage` the conversion happens lazily on first use, so startup does no extra work.
- If the primary key is unavailable for a session, names are hashed with the fallback key; each entry carries a timestamp, so the newest value wins once the primary key is back, and removals made meanwhile are applied.
- Values you write directly to `PlayxSecurePrefs.securePrefs` bypass playx and keep plain names. playx still reads them as a fallback.

## Web

On web every storage type except `memory` uses `encryptedPrefs` with a **non-extractable WebCrypto key** stored in IndexedDB:

- Nothing secret ships with your app: there is no password, salt or key to configure.
- Scripts can use the key while the page runs, but the browser never lets them read or export its bytes. Stored data can't be decrypted on another machine or offline.
- Values saved by 1.x (which used `flutter_secure_storage` on web) are migrated automatically on the first start.

What it doesn't protect against: code running in your page (for example XSS) and full access to the user's browser profile. For auth tokens on web, prefer `HttpOnly` cookies set by your server.

## Switching an existing app from `flutter_secure_storage`

Values saved with the default backend stay in `flutter_secure_storage`. After changing `storageType`, copy them over:

```dart
await PlayxCore.bootCore(
  securePrefsSettings: const PlayxSecurePrefsSettings(
    storageType: PlayxSecureStorageType.auto,
  ),
);

// Safe to call on every start: once the source is empty it does nothing.
final moved = await PlayxSecurePrefs.migrateFromFlutterSecureStorage();
```

| Parameter | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `from` | `PlayxSecurePrefs.securePrefs` | The `FlutterSecureStorage` holding the data. Pass your own instance if it was created with custom options. |
| `deleteFromSource` | `true` | Delete migrated values from `flutter_secure_storage` afterwards. |

- Keys that already exist in the new backend are kept, because they are newer.
- It returns the number of values copied, and `0` when the current backend is `flutterSecureStorage` itself.
- It understands entries whose names were hidden by `encryptKeys`, and skips playx's own internal keys.
- It **reads** `flutter_secure_storage`, so it runs into any native crash that plugin has on a device. If that is why you are switching, consider doing the migration once, behind your own guard.

## Errors and failures

By default errors are thrown to your code. Set `throwOnError: false` for the lenient behavior:

```dart
const PlayxSecurePrefsSettings(throwOnError: false);
```

| | `throwOnError: true` (default) | `throwOnError: false` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Read fails | throws | logs, returns `null` / the fallback |
| Write, remove or clear fails | throws | logs, does nothing |
| Backend can't be created | `create` throws | logs, uses `memory` |
| Value can't be decrypted (`encryptedPrefs`) | returns `null` (always) | returns `null` |

`auto` and `encryptedPrefs` never throw because a storage is unavailable: they end up on `memory`. Failures are written to the `PLAYX CORE` logger (see [Logging](logging.md)).

## Security notes

- **What is protected.** Values at rest on the device. Other apps and casual file access can't read them.
- **What isn't.** A rooted or compromised device, a debugger attached to your running app, and values while they are in memory.
- **The fallback key is obfuscation**, not secrecy. Treat sessions that use it as lower assurance, and prefer a backend that passes its health check.
- **Don't store what you can avoid storing.** Refresh tokens and short-lived credentials are good fits; long-lived secrets shared by all users belong on your server.

See also: [Preferences](preferences.md), [Secure env](secure-env.md) (for secrets that ship *with* the app), [Testing](testing.md).

---

<!-- https://playx-flutter.github.io/playx_core/env/ -->
# Environment configuration

`PlayxEnv` gives your app typed configuration values (API URLs, feature flags, timeouts) from:

1. `.env` files bundled as assets, including one per environment or flavor;
2. build-time values passed with `--dart-define`;
3. [encrypted secure env](secure-env.md) for sensitive values.

All sources are merged into one set of values that you read **synchronously** with typed getters.

> **Security:** `.env` files ship as plain text inside your app and `--dart-define` values are compiled into it. Anyone who has the app can read them. Use them for configuration, and [secure env](secure-env.md) for sensitive values.

- [Quick start](#quick-start)
- [Settings reference](#settings-reference)
- [How values are layered](#how-values-are-layered)
- [Environments and flavors](#environments-and-flavors)
- [File syntax](#file-syntax)
- [Build-time values](#build-time-values)
- [Reading values](#reading-values)
- [Required keys and errors](#required-keys-and-errors)
- [Inspecting what was loaded](#inspecting-what-was-loaded)
- [Loading without `bootCore`](#loading-without-bootcore)
- [Recipes](#recipes)

## Quick start

**1. Create the files** next to your `pubspec.yaml`:

```
# .env
API_URL=https://api.example.com
ENABLE_LOGS=true
TIMEOUT=30s
```

**2. Declare them as assets.** List every file you want to load, including environment files:

```yaml
# pubspec.yaml
flutter:
  assets:
    - .env
    - .env.dev
    - .env.prod
```

**3. Load them at startup** by passing `envSettings` to `bootCore`:

```dart
await PlayxCore.bootCore(
  envSettings: const PlayxEnvSettings(
    requiredKeys: ['API_URL'],   // fail at startup if missing
  ),
);
```

**4. Read values:**

```dart
final apiUrl = PlayxEnv.getUri('API_URL', fallback: Uri.parse('https://api.example.com'));
final logs = PlayxEnv.getBool('ENABLE_LOGS');
final timeout = PlayxEnv.getDuration('TIMEOUT', fallback: const Duration(seconds: 30));
```

## Settings reference

`PlayxEnvSettings` is a `const` class. Every option is optional.

| Option | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `fileName` | `'.env'` | The base file. |
| `environment` | `null` | Environment name (`dev`, `prod`…). Loads `'$fileName.$environment'` after the base file. When `null`, resolved from `--dart-define=PLAYX_ENV`, then the Flutter flavor. |
| `useFlavor` | `true` | Use the Flutter flavor as the environment when none is set. |
| `additionalFiles` | `[]` | More files loaded after the environment file, e.g. `['.env.local']`. |
| `mergeWith` | `{}` | Values that override the files. |
| `usePlayxDefines` | `true` | Read `--dart-define=PLAYX_DEFINES`. |
| `dartDefines` | `{}` | Individual build-time values that override everything else. |
| `secureEnv` | `null` | Encrypted values from [secure env](secure-env.md). |
| `useSecureDefines` | `true` | Read `--dart-define=PLAYX_SECURE_DEFINES`. |
| `requiredKeys` | `[]` | Keys that must have a non-empty value once loaded. |
| `isOptional` | `true` | When `false`, a missing file throws instead of being skipped. |
| `parser` | `Parser()` | The `flutter_dotenv` parser, if you need custom parsing. |

## How values are layered

Sources are applied in this order. **Later sources override earlier ones**, key by key: a source only replaces the keys it defines, everything else is kept.

| # | Source | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `fileName` | `.env` |
| 2 | `'$fileName.$environment'` | `.env.prod` |
| 3 | `additionalFiles`, in order | `.env.local` |
| 4 | [Secure env](secure-env.md): `secureEnv`, then `PLAYX_SECURE_DEFINES` | generated file |
| 5 | `mergeWith` | `{'API_URL': '...'}` |
| 6 | `PLAYX_DEFINES` | `--dart-define=PLAYX_DEFINES="DEBUG=true"` |
| 7 | `dartDefines` | `--dart-define=DEBUG=true` |

```
# .env                            # .env.prod
BASE_URL=https://api.example.com  BASE_URL=https://api.prod.example.com
TIMEOUT=30s
```

With `--dart-define=PLAYX_ENV=prod`, `BASE_URL` comes from `.env.prod` and `TIMEOUT` still comes from `.env`. A `--dart-define=PLAYX_DEFINES="BASE_URL=https://staging.example.com"` on top would replace `BASE_URL` only.

**Missing files.** A missing file is logged and skipped, so a missing `.env.prod` simply leaves the values from `.env` in place. With `isOptional: false`, `load` throws a `PlayxEnvException` listing the missing files. The setting applies to all files at once.

## Environments and flavors

The environment name selects `.env.<name>`. It is resolved in this order:

1. `PlayxEnvSettings.environment`, if set;
2. `--dart-define=PLAYX_ENV=<name>`;
3. the Flutter flavor (`flutter run --flavor <name>`), unless `useFlavor: false`.

```sh
flutter run --dart-define=PLAYX_ENV=dev
flutter run --flavor prod                  # flavors need native flavor setup
flutter build apk --flavor staging
```

`PlayxEnv.environment` reports the resolved name and `PlayxEnv.loadedFiles` the files that were actually found. If no name is resolved, only the base file (and `additionalFiles`) is loaded.

Set `environment` in code when the name comes from somewhere else:

```dart
PlayxEnvSettings(environment: kReleaseMode ? 'prod' : 'dev')
```

## File syntax

Files use the usual `.env` format:

```
# Comments start with a hash
APP_NAME=Playx Core
GREETING="Hello, world"        # quotes keep spaces
export TOKEN_URL=https://auth.example.com
API_URL=https://$HOST/api      # references an earlier value
PRICE=\$5                      # escape a literal dollar sign
```

- Variables can reference earlier values with `$NAME`, including values from earlier **files**.
- **A reference is resolved when its line is read.** If `.env` defines `API_URL=https://$HOST/api` and `.env.prod` only changes `HOST`, `API_URL` keeps the old host. Redefine `API_URL` in `.env.prod` as well.
- Empty files are fine; unreadable lines are ignored.

## Build-time values

Dart can only read a define whose name is written as a **constant in code**. Reading one by a name known only at runtime works in debug builds, but returns `""` in release builds and throws on web, so playx never does that. There are two ways to pass build-time values.

### `PLAYX_DEFINES`: any number of values, nothing to declare

```sh
flutter run --dart-define=PLAYX_DEFINES="DEBUG=true;API_URL=https://dev.example.com"
```

```dart
PlayxEnv.getBool('DEBUG');   // true, with no setup in code
```

- Entries use `.env` syntax, separated by `;` or new lines.
- For values containing `;` or awkward characters, pass base64: `--dart-define=PLAYX_DEFINES=base64:$(base64 < .env.ci)`.
- It works with `--dart-define-from-file`, which avoids shell quoting:

  ```json
  { "PLAYX_DEFINES": "DEBUG=true;API_URL=https://dev.example.com" }
  ```

- Values can reference values from the files (`API_URL=https://$HOST`).
- An explicit empty entry (`KEY=`) overrides with an empty string, which is the only way to blank a value from the command line.
- Disable with `usePlayxDefines: false`.

### `dartDefines`: individual, declared defines

```sh
flutter run --dart-define=DEBUG=true
```

```dart
const PlayxEnvSettings(
  dartDefines: {'DEBUG': String.fromEnvironment('DEBUG')},
);
```

Unset defines come through as `''` and are ignored, so `.env` values stay in place. `dartDefines` wins over `PLAYX_DEFINES`.

> If you only need a flag **in code**, `const debug = bool.fromEnvironment('DEBUG');` is a compile-time constant: code behind `if (debug)` is removed from release builds, which runtime configuration can't do.

## Reading values

All getters are synchronous. Each type has `maybeGetX` (returns `null` when there's no usable value) and `getX` (returns a fallback).

| Type | Accepted values | Read | Fallback default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `String` | anything | `maybeGetString`, `getString` | `''` |
| `int` | `3`, `"3.9"` (truncated) | `maybeGetInt`, `getInt` | `-1` |
| `double` | `2.5`, `3` | `maybeGetDouble`, `getDouble` | `-1` |
| `num` | `7`, `2.5` | `maybeGetNum`, `getNum` | `-1` |
| `bool` | `true`, `false`, `1`, `0` (case-insensitive) | `maybeGetBool`, `getBool` | `false` |
| `Uri` | `https://example.com/a` | `maybeGetUri`, `getUri` | required `fallback` |
| enum | the value's name, case-insensitive | `maybeGetEnum(key, Mode.values)`, `getEnum` | required `fallback` |
| `Duration` | `250ms`, `30s`, `5m`, `1.5h`, `1d` (no unit = milliseconds) | `maybeGetDuration`, `getDuration` | required `fallback` |
| `List<T>` | `a, b, c` or `[1, 2, 3]` | `maybeGetList<T>`, `getList<T>` | `[]` |
| JSON object | `{"enabled": true}` | `maybeGetMap`, `getMap` | `{}` |
| your type | JSON | `maybeGetObject(key, fromJson:)`, `getObject` | required `fallback` |

A value that can't be converted (for example `maybe` as a bool) is treated like a missing one.

```dart
final retries = PlayxEnv.getInt('RETRIES', fallback: 3);
final mode = PlayxEnv.getEnum('THEME_MODE', ThemeMode.values, fallback: ThemeMode.system);
final locales = PlayxEnv.getList<String>('SUPPORTED_LOCALES');       // 'en, ar' -> ['en', 'ar']
final ports = PlayxEnv.getList<int>('PORTS');                        // '80,443' or '[80, 443]'
final flags = PlayxEnv.getObject(
  'FEATURES',
  fromJson: FeatureFlags.fromJson,                                   // '{"newCheckout": true}'
  fallback: const FeatureFlags(),
);
```

Lists accept a custom `separator` (default `,`), skip empty items, and convert `String`, `int`, `double`, `num`, `bool` and `Uri` items automatically. Pass `fromJson` for other types. If any item can't be converted the whole list reads as `null` (or the fallback).

### `PlayxEnv.values` and `EnvValues`

`PlayxEnv`'s getters are shortcuts for the same getters on `PlayxEnv.values`, an immutable `EnvValues`. You can also wrap any `Map<String, String>`, such as remote config:

```dart
final remote = EnvValues({'NEW_CHECKOUT': 'true', 'LIMIT': '10'});
remote.getBool('NEW_CHECKOUT');   // true
remote.getInt('LIMIT');           // 10
```

## Required keys and errors

```dart
const PlayxEnvSettings(requiredKeys: ['API_URL', 'STRIPE_KEY']);
```

`load` throws a `PlayxEnvException` when:

- a required key is missing or empty: `missingKeys` lists **all** of them;
- a file is missing and `isOptional` is `false`: `missingFiles` lists them;
- [secure env](secure-env.md) values can't be decrypted.

```dart
try {
  await PlayxEnv.load(settings);
} on PlayxEnvException catch (e) {
  print(e.message);        // 'Missing required env keys: API_URL'
  print(e.missingKeys);    // ['API_URL']
}
```

`bootCore` rethrows it, so a misconfigured build fails at startup. Values that did load remain available through `PlayxEnv` even when required keys are missing.

## Inspecting what was loaded

| Member | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `PlayxEnv.isLoaded` | Whether values have been loaded. |
| `PlayxEnv.environment` | The resolved environment name, if any. |
| `PlayxEnv.loadedFiles` | The files that were found, in order. |
| `PlayxEnv.all` | Every value **except** secure ones: safe to log. |
| `PlayxEnv.containsKey(key)` | Whether a key has a value (secure keys included). |
| `PlayxEnv.isSecure(key)` | Whether a key holds a [secure value](secure-env.md). |
| `PlayxEnv.values` | The loaded `EnvValues`. |

Reading before `load` returns no values and logs one warning, which usually means `envSettings` was not passed to `bootCore`.

## Loading without `bootCore`

```dart
await PlayxEnv.load(const PlayxEnvSettings(requiredKeys: ['API_URL']));
```

`loadFromString` loads `.env`-formatted text instead of assets, for configuration fetched at runtime or for tests:

```dart
PlayxEnv.loadFromString(
  'API_URL=https://api.example.com\nRETRIES=3',
  mergeWith: {'RETRIES': '5'},
  requiredKeys: ['API_URL'],
);
```

`PlayxEnv.dispose()` clears everything. See [Testing](testing.md) for `setMockValues`.

## Recipes

**Per-environment API URL**

```
# .env            # .env.dev                       # .env.prod
API_URL=https://api.example.com
                  API_URL=https://dev.example.com  API_URL=https://api.prod.example.com
```

```sh
flutter run --dart-define=PLAYX_ENV=dev
```

**A local override that isn't committed**

```dart
const PlayxEnvSettings(additionalFiles: ['.env.local'])
```

Add `.env.local` to `.gitignore` and to your assets while developing. If it isn't there, it is skipped.

**Feature flags from the command line**

```sh
flutter run --dart-define=PLAYX_DEFINES="NEW_CHECKOUT=true;MAX_UPLOADS=5"
```

```dart
if (PlayxEnv.getBool('NEW_CHECKOUT')) { /* ... */ }
```

**Switching the theme from config**

```dart
MaterialApp(
  themeMode: PlayxEnv.getEnum('THEME_MODE', ThemeMode.values, fallback: ThemeMode.system),
);
```

See the [example app](https://github.com/playx-flutter/playx_core/tree/main/example) for a complete project, and [Secure env](secure-env.md) for sensitive values.

---

<!-- https://playx-flutter.github.io/playx_core/secure-env/ -->
# Secure env

Secure env keeps sensitive configuration values (API keys, client secrets, DSNs) **out of plain sight** in your shipped app. You write them in a normal gitignored file, a command encrypts them into a generated Dart file, and `PlayxEnv` decrypts them in memory at startup.

- [What it protects (and what it doesn't)](#what-it-protects-and-what-it-doesnt)
- [Quick start](#quick-start)
- [How it works](#how-it-works)
- [Writing the secrets files](#writing-the-secrets-files)
- [The `secure_env` command](#the-secure_env-command)
- [Keys](#keys)
- [CI/CD](#cicd)
- [Encrypted define](#encrypted-define-playx_secure_defines)
- [At runtime](#at-runtime)
- [Troubleshooting](#troubleshooting)

## What it protects (and what it doesn't)

Plain `.env` assets and `--dart-define` values end up in your app as readable text. Anyone can unzip an APK or IPA, run `strings` on the binary, open browser devtools on a web build, or point an automated scanner at it, and read them.

Secure env removes that: **names and values are encrypted together and stored as numbers**, never as strings, so none of those techniques find anything.

| Threat | Protected? |
| --- | --- |
| Unzipping the app, `strings`, asset inspection | **Yes** |
| Automated scanners that look for API keys in published apps | **Yes** |
| Secrets committed to git by accident | **Yes**: only the encrypted file and the (gitignored) key exist |
| Someone reverse engineering your app with a debugger or decompiler | **No**: the app has to decrypt the values itself, so the key ships with it |

> **The honest limit:** anything an app can decrypt on its own, a determined attacker who has the app can decrypt too. Secure env raises the bar from "anyone with unzip" to "a motivated reverse engineer". For keys that would cause real damage if leaked, don't put them in the app at all: keep them on your server (or a serverless function) and let the app call that instead.

## Quick start

**1. Put secrets in a gitignored file.**

```
# .env.secrets
STRIPE_KEY=pk_test_123
MAPS_API_KEY=AIza...
```

**2. Generate the encrypted Dart file.**

```sh
dart run playx:secure_env
```

> Apps using the `playx` package run `dart run playx:secure_env`; apps depending on `playx_core` only run `dart run playx_core:secure_env`. Both take the same options. The examples in this guide use `playx:secure_env`.

This writes `lib/generated/playx_secure_env.g.dart` and creates a key in `.playx_secure_env.key`.

**3. Ignore the secrets and the key.**

```
# .gitignore
.env.secrets*
.playx_secure_env.key
lib/generated/playx_secure_env.g.dart
secure_defines.json
```

**4. Pass the generated value to `PlayxEnv`.**

```dart
import 'generated/playx_secure_env.g.dart';

await PlayxCore.bootCore(
  envSettings: const PlayxEnvSettings(
    secureEnv: playxSecureEnv,
    requiredKeys: ['STRIPE_KEY'],
  ),
);

PlayxEnv.getString('STRIPE_KEY');   // 'pk_test_123'
PlayxEnv.isSecure('STRIPE_KEY');    // true
```

Secure values use the same getters as every other value (`getString`, `getInt`, `getUri`…), see [Environment configuration](env.md#reading-values).

## How it works

```
.env.secrets  ──►  secure_env command  ──►  playx_secure_env.g.dart  ──►  PlayxEnv.load()
 (gitignored)       AES-256-GCM            encrypted blob + split key     decrypts in memory
```

- **One encrypted blob.** The whole map (names and values) is serialized, then encrypted with **AES-256-GCM** under a fresh random nonce. GCM also authenticates the data, so tampering is detected.
- **Stored as numbers.** The generated file holds the blob as integer lists, so nothing appears as a string in the compiled app.
- **Split key.** The key is stored as two byte lists that are XOR-ed back together at runtime, so it never appears as one contiguous value. (This is obfuscation, see [the limit above](#what-it-protects-and-what-it-doesnt).)
- **Layering.** Secure values are applied after the `.env` files and before `mergeWith`, `PLAYX_DEFINES` and `dartDefines`, so those can still override a secret, for example for local testing. See [How values are layered](env.md#how-values-are-layered).
- **Hidden from dumps.** Secure values are excluded from `PlayxEnv.all`, so logging your configuration doesn't leak them. The getters still return them.

## Writing the secrets files

Secrets files use the same syntax as [`.env` files](env.md#file-syntax): comments, quotes, `export`, and `$VAR` references.

| File | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `.env.secrets` | Secrets for every environment. |
| `.env.secrets.<env>` | Secrets for one environment, overriding the base file. Read when `--env <env>` is passed. |

```
# .env.secrets                  # .env.secrets.prod
STRIPE_KEY=pk_test_123          STRIPE_KEY=pk_live_987
MAPS_API_KEY=AIza-dev
```

```sh
dart run playx:secure_env --env prod
```

generates a file for `prod` containing `STRIPE_KEY=pk_live_987` and `MAPS_API_KEY=AIza-dev`. A build only contains the secrets of the environment it was generated for, so a production build never ships development secrets.

Regenerate the file whenever you change a secrets file or switch environment.

## The `secure_env` command

```
dart run playx:secure_env [command] [options]
```

### Commands

| Command | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `generate` (default) | Writes the encrypted Dart file used with `PlayxEnvSettings(secureEnv: playxSecureEnv)`. |
| `define` | Prints (or writes with `--out`) the encrypted value of the `PLAYX_SECURE_DEFINES` define. See [below](#encrypted-define-playx_secure_defines). |
| `generate-key` | Prints a new random key, for example to store as a CI secret. |
| `--help` | Shows all options. |

### Where values come from

Sources are applied in this order; later ones override earlier ones.

| Option | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `--input <file>` | The secrets file. Default `.env.secrets`. A missing explicit input is an error. |
| `--env <name>` | Also read `<input>.<name>`. Defaults to the `PLAYX_ENV` environment variable. |
| `--no-file` | Don't read secrets files (CI with variables only). |
| `--from-env A,B` | Read these environment variables. An unset one is an error. |
| `--from-env-prefix P` | Read every environment variable starting with `P`, without the prefix (`PLAYX_SECRET_API_KEY` becomes `API_KEY`). |
| `--define KEY=VALUE` | Add a value. Repeatable. |
| `--allow-empty` | Don't fail when there are no values at all. |

### Key options

| Option | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `--key <base64>` | Use this key. |
| `PLAYX_ENV_KEY` | Environment variable holding the key. |
| `--key-file <file>` | Where the key is kept. Default `.playx_secure_env.key`. Created if missing. |
| `--rotate-key` | Create a new key and overwrite the key file. |

The first available of these is used, in this order: `--key`, `PLAYX_ENV_KEY`, the key file; otherwise a new key is generated and saved to the key file.

### Output options

| Option | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `--output <file>` | The generated Dart file. Default `lib/generated/playx_secure_env.g.dart`. |
| `--key-from-define` | Don't embed the key; the build passes it with `--dart-define=PLAYX_ENV_KEY=<key>`. See [Keys](#keys). |
| `--import <uri>` | The import used by the generated file. Default `package:playx/playx.dart` when the project depends on `playx`, otherwise `package:playx_core/playx_core.dart`. |
| `--out <file.json>` | `define` only: write a `--dart-define-from-file` JSON file (existing keys in the file are kept). |
| `--verbose` | Print the *names* of the values and the sources used. Never prints values. |

### Behavior worth knowing

- Output never contains secret values. The command prints counts, and key names only with `--verbose`.
- It warns when a secrets file, the key file, or a generated file that embeds the key is **not** in `.gitignore` (when run inside a git repository).
- Exit codes: `0` success, `1` failure (missing input, unset variable, invalid key…), `64` usage error. CI builds therefore fail when something is wrong.
- The generated file starts with `// dart format off`, so formatting your project doesn't expand it into thousands of lines.

## Keys

| Mode | How | Pros | Cons |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Embedded** (default) | The key is generated once, saved in `.playx_secure_env.key`, and embedded (split) in the generated file. | Nothing to configure at build time. Not visible as a string in the binary. | The generated file contains the key: keep it out of git. |
| **From a define** | `--key-from-define`; build with `--dart-define=PLAYX_ENV_KEY=<key>`. | The generated file holds only ciphertext and can be committed. | `--dart-define` values are compiled into the app as readable strings, so this keeps the key out of **git**, not out of the **app**. |

When both are present, the embedded key is used first.

- **Rotate** with `--rotate-key` and regenerate. Every previously generated file stops working with the new key, so regenerate them all together.
- **Create a key** for CI with `dart run playx:secure_env generate-key`.
- **Reuse a key** across machines by setting `PLAYX_ENV_KEY` (or `--key`) when generating.

## CI/CD

CI machines have no gitignored `.env.secrets`; secrets live in the platform's settings and reach the build as **environment variables**. Run one command before `flutter build`:

```sh
PLAYX_ENV=prod \
PLAYX_SECRET_STRIPE_KEY=... PLAYX_SECRET_MAPS_API_KEY=... \
dart run playx:secure_env --from-env-prefix PLAYX_SECRET_

flutter build appbundle --release
```

- `PLAYX_ENV` selects the environment (and matches the runtime `PLAYX_ENV` define if you use it).
- Every `PLAYX_SECRET_<NAME>` variable becomes `<NAME>`, so **adding a secret is a dashboard change only**, with no edit to the build script.
- The key is created inside the job and embedded in the generated file, which is used by that same build. Nothing else to manage.
- Prefer `--from-env STRIPE_KEY,MAPS_API_KEY` or `--define KEY=VALUE` if you want explicit names.

Ready-made configurations, copy and adapt:

| Platform | File |
| --- | --- |
| Codemagic | [`doc/ci/codemagic.yaml`](ci/codemagic.yaml) |
| GitHub Actions | [`doc/ci/github-actions.yml`](ci/github-actions.yml) |
| Vercel (Flutter web) | [`doc/ci/vercel.json`](ci/vercel.json) and [`doc/ci/vercel-build.sh`](ci/vercel-build.sh) |

Any other CI follows the same pattern: expose secrets as `PLAYX_SECRET_*` variables, run the command, then build.

**Web hosts.** A web build is a public JavaScript bundle. Secure env keeps values out of plain sight, but for keys that must stay secret, call a serverless function (for example Vercel `api/`) that holds the key and talks to the third-party service for your app.

## Encrypted define (`PLAYX_SECURE_DEFINES`)

An alternative to the generated file's data: pass the encrypted values as a build define, so they can change without regenerating Dart code.

```sh
dart run playx:secure_env define --from-env-prefix PLAYX_SECRET_ --out secure_defines.json
flutter build apk --dart-define-from-file=secure_defines.json
```

`secure_defines.json` contains only ciphertext:

```json
{ "PLAYX_SECURE_DEFINES": "v1:..." }
```

- The app decrypts it with the same key, which comes from the generated file (generate it in the same job, with the same key) or from `PLAYX_ENV_KEY`.
- Defines override the generated values, so you can ship a base file and adjust per build.
- Disable reading it with `PlayxEnvSettings(useSecureDefines: false)`.
- The define is ciphertext, so finding it in the binary is useless without the key.

Most apps don't need this; the CI flow above is simpler.

## At runtime

| Situation | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Normal | Values are decrypted in memory and served by the usual getters. They are excluded from `PlayxEnv.all`. |
| No key available, wrong key, or tampered data | `PlayxEnv.load` throws a `PlayxEnvException` (a build misconfiguration that should fail at startup or in CI). The message never includes values. |
| Generated for another environment | A warning is logged, for example "generated for `prod` but the environment is `dev`". Values are still loaded. |
| A required key is missing after decrypting | `PlayxEnvException` with `missingKeys`. |

## Troubleshooting

| Message | Cause and fix |
| --- | --- |
| `No secret values found` | The secrets file doesn't exist or is empty, and no `--from-env`, `--from-env-prefix` or `--define` supplied values. Create the file, or pass `--allow-empty`. |
| `Input file … not found` | `--input` points at a missing file. |
| `Environment variable X is not set` | A name given to `--from-env` isn't exported in the shell. |
| `Warning: no environment variables start with …` | `--from-env-prefix` matched nothing: check the prefix and that the CI variables are exposed to the step. |
| `Warning: … is not in .gitignore` | Add the file to `.gitignore` before committing. |
| `Secure env values could not be decrypted` | The key in the app doesn't match the data, or the data was altered. Regenerate the file, and make sure `--rotate-key` wasn't run for only some artifacts. |
| `…there is no key` | The generated file was created with `--key-from-define` and the build didn't pass `--dart-define=PLAYX_ENV_KEY=<key>`. |
| `Secure env was generated for "prod" but the environment is "dev"` | You built with a file generated for another environment. Regenerate with the right `--env`. |
| The command isn't found | Use `dart run playx_core:secure_env` when your app depends on `playx_core` only, and `dart run playx:secure_env` when it depends on `playx`. |

See also: [Environment configuration](env.md), the [example app](https://github.com/playx-flutter/playx_core/tree/main/example), and [Testing](testing.md).

---

<!-- https://playx-flutter.github.io/playx_core/extensions/ -->
# Extensions

Everything here is available from `import 'package:playx_core/playx_core.dart';`.

- [String](#string)
- [Iterable](#iterable)
- [DateTime](#datetime)
- [Duration](#duration)
- [Color](#color)
- [bool](#bool)
- [Locale](#locale)
- [Future](#future)
- [BuildContext](#buildcontext)
- [Padding](#padding)
- [Borders and radius](#borders-and-radius)

## String

### Formatting and case

| Member | Does | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `capitalizeFirstChar` | Uppercases the first character. | `'hello'` → `'Hello'` |
| `capitalizeFirstCharForEachWord` | Uppercases the first character of every space-separated word. | `'hello big world'` → `'Hello Big World'` |
| `capitalizedInitialChar` | The first visible character, uppercased. Unicode-safe (emoji and combined characters stay whole); empty for blank strings. Ideal for avatar initials. | `'  élodie'` → `'É'` |
| `format(List args)` | `sprintf`-style formatting. | `'Hi %s, you are %d'.format(['Jane', 30])` |
| `limit(maxLength, {suffix})` | Truncates and appends a suffix (default `...`). | `'Hello World'.limit(5)` → `'Hello...'` |
| `toSlug()` | URL-friendly slug. | `'Hello, World! 2024'` → `'hello-world-2024'` |
| `toPrettyJson({indent})` | Indents a JSON string; returns it unchanged if it isn't valid JSON. | `'{"a":1}'` → `'{\n  "a": 1\n}'` |

### Inspecting and searching

| Member | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `reversed` | The characters in reverse order. |
| `isPalindrome` | Whether the string equals its reverse. |
| `linesCount` | Number of lines. |
| `firstOrNull`, `lastOrNull`, `lastOrEmpty` | First / last character, or `null` / `''` when empty. |
| `containsIgnoreCase(other)`, `equalsIgnoreCase(other)` | Case-insensitive comparison. |
| `anyChar(predicate)` | Whether any single character satisfies the predicate. |
| `isNumeric` | Whether it parses as a number. |
| `isValidEmail`, `isValidUrl` | Basic format checks (not a guarantee that the address or URL exists). |

### Converting and editing

| Member | Does | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `toBoolean()` | `true` for `'true'` or `'1'` (case-insensitive), otherwise `false`. | `'TRUE'.toBoolean()` → `true` |
| `toIntOrNull()`, `toDoubleOrNull()` | Parse, or `null`. | `'42'.toIntOrNull()` → `42` |
| `removeWhitespace()` | Removes all whitespace. | `' a b '` → `'ab'` |
| `removeHtmlTags()` | Strips basic HTML tags. | `'<b>Hi</b>'` → `'Hi'` |
| `replaceAfter(delimiter, replacement, [defaultValue])` | Replaces everything after the first `delimiter` (the delimiter stays). | `'key=old'.replaceAfter('=', 'new')` → `'key=new'` |
| `replaceBefore(delimiter, replacement, [defaultValue])` | Replaces everything before the first `delimiter`. | `'old=value'.replaceBefore('=', 'new')` → `'new=value'` |

For safer conversions of unknown values see [`toIntOrNull`/`toInt`… in Utilities](utilities.md#safe-conversion).

### Nullable strings

```dart
String? name;
name.isNullOrEmpty;              // true
name.isNotNullOrEmpty;           // false
name.ifNullOrEmpty('Anonymous'); // 'Anonymous'
```

## Iterable

Methods are on every `Iterable<T>` (lists, sets…). Note `firstOrNull()` and `lastOrNull()` are **methods**.

### Counting and picking

| Member | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `countWhere([predicate])` | Number of elements matching (all elements without a predicate). |
| `countNotNull()` | Number of non-null elements. |
| `random` | A random element, or `null` when empty. |
| `firstOrNull()`, `lastOrNull()` | First / last element, or `null`. |
| `firstOr(value)`, `lastOr(value)` | First / last element, or `value`. |
| `isIndexValid(index)` | Whether `index` is in range. |
| `atOrNull(index)`, `atOr(index, value)` | Element at `index`, or `null` / `value`. |
| `firstWhereOrNull(test)`, `firstWhereOr(test, value)` | First match, or `null` / `value`. |
| `lastWhereOrNull(test)`, `lastWhereOr(test, value)` | Last match, or `null` / `value`. |

### Transforming

| Member | Does | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `withoutDuplicate()` | List without duplicates. | `[1, 1, 2]` → `[1, 2]` |
| `mapWithIndex((i, e) => …)` | Map with the index. | `['a', 'b']` → `['0a', '1b']` |
| `chunked(size)` | Splits into lists of `size` (throws `ArgumentError` for `size <= 0`). | `[1, 2, 3].chunked(2)` → `[[1, 2], [3]]` |
| `groupBy(keySelector)` | `Map<K, List<T>>`. | `[1, 2, 3].groupBy((e) => e.isEven)` |
| `sortedBy(key)`, `sortedByDescending(key)` | A sorted copy (the source is untouched). | `words.sortedBy((w) => w.length)` |

### Asynchronous mapping

```dart
final doubled = await [1, 2, 3].asyncMap(mapper: (e) async => e * 2);
final parsed = await files.asyncMapInIsolate(mapper: parseFile);   // runs each item in an isolate
```

`asyncMapInIsolate` takes `useWorkManager` (use the `worker_manager` pool started by `bootCore`, default `true`), `printError` and `printEachItemError`. The mapper must be a top-level or static function (it is sent to another isolate). See also [`MapUtils`](utilities.md#maputils-and-mapasync).

### Nested iterables

```dart
final nested = [[1, 2], [3], <int>[]];
nested.flatten();                                      // [1, 2, 3]
nested.flatMap(mapper: (e) => e * 10);                 // 10, 20, 30
await nested.flatMapAsync(mapper: (e) async => e + 1); // [2, 3, 4]
```

`asyncFlatMap` is deprecated; use `flatMapAsync`.

### Numbers

```dart
[1, 2, 3, 4].sum;       // 10
[1, 2, 3, 4].average;   // 2.5
<int>[].sum;            // 0 (empty collections give 0)
```

## DateTime

| Member | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `isAm` | Whether the hour is before 12. |
| `nextDay`, `previousDay` | ±1 day. |
| `sameDayNextWeek`, `sameDayPreviousWeek` | ±7 days. |
| `nextMonth`, `previousMonth` | **±30 days**, not a calendar month. |
| `isToday`, `isTomorrow`, `isYesterday` | Relative to now. |
| `isSameDay(date)`, `isSameMonth(date)`, `isSameYear(date)` | Compare calendar parts. |
| `isSameWeek(date: …, firstDay: …)` | Same week, for a configurable first weekday. |
| `isInThisWeek({firstDay})`, `isInThisMonth`, `isInThisYear` | Relative to now. |
| `isInTheFuture`, `isInThePast` | Compared with now. |
| `dayOfTheWeekIndex({firstDay})` | 0-6, counted from `firstDay` (default Monday). |
| `dayOfTheWeek()` → `Weekday`, `monthOfTheYear()` → `Month` | Enums with a `fromDate` constructor. |
| `isLeapYear` | Leap-year check. |
| `withoutTime()` | Midnight of the same day. |
| `copyWith({year, month, day, hour, minute, second, millisecond})` | Replace parts. |
| `startOfDay`, `endOfDay` | `00:00:00.000` / `23:59:59.999`. |
| `startOfMonth`, `endOfMonth` | First moment / last millisecond of the month. |
| `startOfWeek({firstDay})`, `endOfWeek({firstDay})` | Boundaries of the week; Monday-first by default. |

```dart
final date = DateTime(2024, 5, 15);          // a Wednesday
date.startOfWeek();                           // 2024-05-13
date.startOfWeek(firstDay: Weekday.sunday);   // 2024-05-12
date.endOfMonth;                              // 2024-05-31 23:59:59.999
date.dayOfTheWeek();                          // Weekday.wednesday
```

## Duration

Total and remaining parts, as strings with an optional leading zero (default `true`):

| Member | Example for `27h 5m 9s` |
| --- | --- |
| `toDays()`, `toHours()`, `toMinutes()`, `toSeconds()`, `toMilliSeconds()` | `toHours()` → `'27'` (total hours) |
| `toRemainingHours()`, `toRemainingMinutes()`, `toRemainingSeconds()` | `'03'`, `'05'`, `'09'` |
| `toFormattedDuration(...)` | see below |
| `delay([callback])` | Waits for the duration, then runs `callback` (if given) and returns its result |

```dart
const d = Duration(hours: 27, minutes: 5, seconds: 9);

d.toRemainingMinutes();                            // '05'
d.toRemainingMinutes(leadingZero: false);          // '5'

d.toFormattedDuration(
  days: 'd', hours: 'h', minutes: 'm', seconds: 's', spacer: ', ',
);                                                  // '01 d, 03 h, 05 m, 09 s'

await const Duration(seconds: 2).delay(() => 'done');   // 'done' after 2 seconds
```

Parts you don't pass (`days:`, `hours:`…) are left out. `leaveSpaceBetweenTimeAndText: false` removes the space (`'3h5m'`). `twoDigits(int)` is also exported.

## Color

```dart
const color = Color(0xFF336699);

color.toHex();                               // '#336699'
color.toHex(leadingHashSign: false);         // '336699'
color.toHex(includeAlpha: true);             // '#ff336699'

PlayxColorExtensions.fromHex('#336699');     // Color(0xFF336699)
PlayxColorExtensions.fromHex('80336699');    // with alpha

color.copyWith(alpha: 0.5, red: 1);          // channels are 0.0-1.0
color.lighten(0.2);                          // lightness +0.2, clamped
color.darken();                              // lightness -0.1 by default
color.isDark;                                // luminance < 0.5: pick a text color
```

`ColorUtils.fromHex(hex:, alpha:)` and `ColorUtils.fromRGB(...)` are also available, see [Utilities](utilities.md#colors).

## bool

```dart
true.toInt();        // 1
false.toInt();       // 0
true.toggle();       // false

bool? value;
value.isTrue;        // true only for an explicit true
value.isFalse;       // true only for an explicit false
```

## Locale

| Member | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `isRTL` | Right-to-left languages: Arabic, Farsi, Hebrew, Pashto, Urdu. |
| `direction` | The matching `TextDirection`. |
| `isArabic`, `isEnglish` | Language checks. |

## Future

```dart
final length = await fetchName().map((name) => name.length);
```

`map` transforms the result of a future (`FutureOr` transform allowed).

## BuildContext

### Theme

| Member | Same as |
| --- | --- |
| `theme`, `textTheme`, `brightness` | `Theme.of(context)`, `.textTheme`, `.brightness` |
| `isDark`, `isLight` | whether the brightness is dark / light |

### Colors

Shortcuts for `Theme.of(context)` colors: `primaryColor`, `primaryColorDark`, `primaryColorLight`, `backgroundColor`, `scaffoldBackgroundColor`, `bottomAppBarColor`, `cardColor`, `dividerColor`, `disabledColor`, `focusColor`, `hoverColor`, `highlightColor`, `splashColor`, `unselectedWidgetColor`, `secondaryHeaderColor`, `hintColor`, `errorColor`, `colorScheme`, `secondary`, `buttonPrimaryColor`.

And every Material 3 `ColorScheme` role: `primary`, `onPrimary`, `primaryContainer`, `onPrimaryContainer`, `secondary` (+ `on…`, `…Container`), `tertiary` (+ `on…`, `…Container`), `surface`, `onSurface`, `error`, `onError`, `errorContainer`, `onErrorContainer`, `outline`, `outlineVariant`, `shadow`, `scrim`, `inverseSurface`, `onInverseSurface`, `inversePrimary`.

```dart
Container(color: context.primaryContainer, child: Text('Hi', style: TextStyle(color: context.onPrimaryContainer)));
```

### Media query

| Member | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `mediaQuery` | `MediaQuery.of(context)` |
| `width`, `height`, `aspectRatio` | Screen size values |
| `mediaQueryPadding` | System padding (notches, bars) |
| `orientation`, `isPortrait`, `isLandscape` | Orientation |
| `alwaysUse24HourFormat` | The platform setting |
| `crossAxisCount({mediumBreakpoint, wideBreakpoint, compact, medium, wide})` | Grid columns for the width: `1` below 840, `2` from 840, `3` from 1400 |

```dart
GridView.count(crossAxisCount: context.crossAxisCount(), children: items);
context.crossAxisCount(mediumBreakpoint: 600, medium: 3, wide: 5);
```

> **`context.size` is not the screen size.** `BuildContext` already has a member named `size` (the size of the widget's render object), and a real member wins over an extension getter. Use `context.width`, `context.height` and `context.aspectRatio` for the screen.

### Navigation

| Member | Same as |
| --- | --- |
| `navigator`, `rootNavigator` | `Navigator.of(context)` / `…, rootNavigator: true` |
| `canPop` | `Navigator.of(context).canPop()` |
| `pop()` | `Navigator.of(context).pop()` |
| `focusScope` | `FocusScope.of(context)` |
| `form` | `Form.maybeOf(context)`: `null` when there is no `Form` above |

### Localization

`directionality`, `isRtl`, `isLtr`, `locale`.

## Padding

Helpers to create `EdgeInsets` from numbers, and to wrap widgets in `Padding`. Values are unscaled (see [conventions](README.md#conventions-used-in-these-guides)).

### On numbers

| Member | Creates |
| --- | --- |
| `p`, `pAll` | `EdgeInsets.all(n)` |
| `px`, `pLR` | `EdgeInsets.symmetric(horizontal: n)` |
| `py`, `pTB` | `EdgeInsets.symmetric(vertical: n)` |
| `pt`, `pb`, `pl`, `pr` | One side: top, bottom, left, right |
| `ps`, `pe` | `EdgeInsetsDirectional` start / end (follows RTL) |
| `pZero` | `EdgeInsets.zero` |

```dart
Container(padding: 16.p);
Container(padding: 8.px + 4.py);          // insets add up
Container(padding: 12.ps);                // start side: left in LTR, right in RTL
```

Insets of the same kind combine with `+`. To mix absolute and directional insets, use `add`, which returns an `EdgeInsetsGeometry` resolved against the text direction:

```dart
Container(padding: 12.ps.add(4.pt));      // start 12 + top 4
```

### On widgets

| Member | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `withPadding(EdgeInsetsGeometry)` | Wrap with any padding, e.g. `16.px`. |
| `pAll(value)` | Equal padding on all sides. |
| `pSymmetric({horizontal, vertical})` | Symmetric padding. |
| `pOnly({left, top, right, bottom})` | Per-side padding. |
| `pDirectional({start, top, end, bottom})` | RTL-aware padding. |
| `pZero()` | `EdgeInsets.zero`: a placeholder padding. |

```dart
Text('Hello').pAll(16);
Text('Hello').pSymmetric(horizontal: 12, vertical: 6);
Text('Hello').pDirectional(start: 8);
Text('Hello').withPadding(24.px);
```

All of them return a `Padding`.

## Borders and radius

### On numbers

| Member | Creates |
| --- | --- |
| `radius` | `Radius.circular(n)` |
| `ellipticalRadius(y)` | `Radius.elliptical(n, y)` |
| `borderRadius` | `BorderRadius.circular(n)` |
| `borderRadiusTop`, `borderRadiusBottom`, `borderRadiusLeft`, `borderRadiusRight` | Rounded on one side |
| `borderRadiusStart`, `borderRadiusEnd` | `BorderRadiusDirectional` start / end (RTL-aware) |
| `roundedShape` | `RoundedRectangleBorder`, e.g. for `Card.shape` |
| `border([color])` | `Border.all(width: n)` |
| `borderSide([color])` | `BorderSide(width: n)` |

```dart
DecoratedBox(
  decoration: BoxDecoration(
    borderRadius: 12.borderRadius,
    border: 1.border(Colors.grey),
  ),
);
Card(shape: 8.roundedShape);
ClipRRect(borderRadius: 16.borderRadiusTop, child: image);
```

### On colors

```dart
Colors.grey.border(width: 2);   // Border.all
Colors.grey.borderSide();       // BorderSide, width 1
```

### On widgets

| Member | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `clipRounded(radius)` | `ClipRRect` with a circular radius. |
| `clipBorderRadius(borderRadius)` | `ClipRRect` with any radius, e.g. `16.borderRadiusTop`. |
| `bordered({color, width, radius})` | Draws a border (rounded when `radius > 0`). |

```dart
Image.network(url).clipRounded(12);
Text('Tag').pSymmetric(horizontal: 8, vertical: 4).bordered(color: Colors.grey, radius: 8);
```
