<!-- https://playx-flutter.github.io/playx_core/utilities/ -->
# Utilities

- [Safe conversion](#safe-conversion)
- [Safe JSON access](#safe-json-access)
- [MapUtils and mapAsync](#maputils-and-mapasync)
- [System UI helpers](#system-ui-helpers)
- [Clipboard](#clipboard)
- [Platform checks](#platform-checks)
- [WebUtils](#webutils)
- [Colors](#colors)
- [Scroll behavior](#scroll-behavior)

## Safe conversion

Functions that turn an unknown value (`dynamic`, for example from JSON or a map) into a typed one **without throwing** unless you ask them to. Every type has three forms:

| Form | Returns |
| --- | --- |
| `toXOrNull(value)` | the converted value, or `null` |
| `toXOr(value, fallback: …)` | the converted value, or the fallback |
| `toX(value)` | the converted value, or throws a `FormatException` |

| Type | Functions | Converts |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `int` | `toIntOrNull`, `toIntOr` (`0`), `toInt` | `int`, `double` (truncated), `bool` (`1`/`0`), numeric `String` (`"3.9"` → `3`) |
| `num` | `toNumOrNull`, `toNumOr`, `toNum` | `num`, `bool`, numeric `String` |
| `double` | `toDoubleOrNull`, `toDoubleOr` (`0.0`), `toDouble` | `double`, `int`, `bool`, numeric `String` |
| `bool` | `toBoolOrNull`, `toBoolOr`, `toBool` | `bool`, `1`/`0`, `'true'`/`'false'`/`'1'`/`'0'` (case-insensitive). Anything else is `null`. |
| `String` | `toStringOrNull`, `toStringOr`, `toString` | `String`, `bool`, `num` |
| `DateTime` | `toDateTimeOrNull`, `toDateTimeOr`, `toDateTime` | `DateTime`, ISO-8601 `String`, epoch milliseconds (`int`) |
| local `DateTime` | `toLocalDateTimeOrNull`, `toLocalDateTimeOr`, `toLocalDateTime` | same, converted to local time; see `utcOffset` below |
| `Map<K, V>` | `toMapOrNull`, `toMapOr`, `toMap` | a `Map<K, V>` (or an empty map) |
| `List<T>` | `toListOrNull`, `toListOr`, `toList` | a `List<T>`; with `fromJson`, each item is converted |
| enum | `toEnumOrNull(value, Mode.values)`, `toEnumOr`, `toEnum` | the enum value whose name matches, case-insensitive |
| `Uri` | `toUriOrNull`, `toUriOr`, `toUri` | `Uri` or a parseable `String` |
| any `T` | `toTOrNull(value, fromJson:)`, `toTOr`, `toT` | runs your `fromJson`; errors become `null` |

```dart
toIntOrNull('42');                          // 42
toIntOrNull('abc');                         // null
toIntOr('abc', fallback: -1);               // -1
toBoolOrNull('TRUE');                       // true
toBoolOrNull('maybe');                      // null
toEnumOrNull('dark', Mode.values);          // Mode.dark
toListOrNull<int>(['1', '2'], fromJson: (e) => int.parse(e as String));  // [1, 2]
toUri('https://example.com');
toInt('abc');                               // throws FormatException
```

### Dates in a fixed time zone

Servers often send local times without a zone, such as `2024-05-01 10:00:00` in Saudi time. Pass the zone's offset to read them correctly:

```dart
const saudi = Duration(hours: 3);
toLocalDateTime('2024-05-01 10:00:00', utcOffset: saudi);   // 07:00 UTC, shown in local time
```

Values that already carry a zone (`Z`, `+03:00`) and epoch integers are absolute and unaffected by `utcOffset`. Without it, a value without a zone is read as local time.

## Safe JSON access

The same conversions, reading a **key** from decoded JSON. Functions are named `asX`, with the same three forms (`asXOrNull`, `asXOr`, `asX`):

```dart
final json = jsonDecode(body);

final name = asString(json, 'name');                       // throws if missing
final age = asIntOr(json, 'age', fallback: 0);
final city = asStringOrNull(json, 'address.city');         // nested key
final firstTag = asStringOrNull(json, 'tags.0');           // list index
final created = asDateTimeOrNull(json, 'createdAt');
final mode = asEnumOr(json, 'mode', Mode.values, fallback: Mode.light);
final tags = asListString(json, 'tags');
final scores = asListInt(json, 'scores');                  // [1, '2', 3.0] -> [1, 2, 3]
final settings = asMapOrNull<String, dynamic>(json, 'settings');
final owner = asTOrNull<User>(json, 'owner', fromJson: User.fromJson);
```

- **Nested keys** use dot notation and list indexes (`'data.users.0.name'`). A key that literally contains a dot is matched first, so `{'a.b': 1}` still works.
- Available types: `int`, `double`, `num`, `bool`, `String`, `DateTime` (and local), enums, `Uri`, `Map`, `List`, `List<int>`, `List<String>`, and any `T` through `asT*`.
- A missing key, a `null` json, or a value that can't be converted all give `null` / the fallback (or a `FormatException` for the throwing form).
- `asLocalDateTime*` accept `utcOffset`, like the `to*` versions.

This pairs well with `fromJson` factories:

```dart
factory User.fromJson(dynamic json) => User(
      name: asString(json, 'name'),
      age: asIntOr(json, 'age'),
      email: asStringOrNull(json, 'contact.email'),
    );
```

## MapUtils and mapAsync

Run a mapping function asynchronously, optionally in an isolate, with built-in error handling.

```dart
// Asynchronously, in the current isolate
final dto = await MapUtils.mapAsync<String, User>(
  data: body,
  mapper: (body) => User.fromJson(jsonDecode(body)),
);

// In an isolate: keeps the UI thread free for heavy parsing
final users = await MapUtils.mapAsyncInIsolate<String, List<User>>(
  data: body,
  mapper: parseUsers,                 // top-level or static function
);

// The same, as an extension on any value
final user = await body.mapAsync(mapper: parseUser);
final list = await body.mapAsyncInIsolate(mapper: parseUsers);
```

| Parameter | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `data`, `mapper` | The input and the function (`FutureOr<S> Function(T)`). |
| `printError` | Log errors with the `PLAYX CORE` logger. Defaults to `kDebugMode`. |
| `onError` | `S Function(T data, Object error, StackTrace stack)`. When given, errors are caught and its return value is returned instead of rethrowing. |
| `useWorkManager` | (`mapAsyncInIsolate`) Run on the `worker_manager` pool started by `bootCore` (default `true`), or with Flutter's `compute` when `false`. |

```dart
final user = await body.mapAsync(
  mapper: parseUser,
  onError: (data, error, stack) => User.guest(),   // never throws
);
```

**Isolate rules.** The mapper and the data are sent to another isolate, so the mapper must be a **top-level or static function** (not a closure capturing objects), and the data and result must be sendable. For lists, see [`asyncMapInIsolate`](extensions.md#asynchronous-mapping).

## System UI helpers

Top-level functions for the status bar, navigation bar, orientation, keyboard and full screen:

| Function | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `setStatusBarColor({color, isDark})` | Status bar color (default transparent). `isDark: true` gives dark icons, for light backgrounds. |
| `setNavigationBarColor({color, isDark})` | Bottom navigation bar color (default black) and icon brightness. |
| `setOrientation({isPortrait, allowRotation})` | Locks the orientation. Portrait only by default; `allowRotation` adds upside-down (portrait) or both directions (landscape). |
| `hideKeyboard()` | Hides the on-screen keyboard. |
| `showKeyboard()` | Asks the system to show it for the focused field. |
| `enterFullScreen()` / `exitFullScreen()` | Immersive mode that hides the system bars, and restores them. |

```dart
setStatusBarColor(color: Colors.white, isDark: true);
setOrientation(isPortrait: false, allowRotation: true);   // landscape, both directions
hideKeyboard();
```

## Clipboard

```dart
await copyToClipboard('hello');
final text = await getClipboardText();      // 'hello', or null when empty
await clearClipboard();
```

## Platform checks

`PlayxPlatform` wraps `defaultTargetPlatform` and `kIsWeb`, so it works on every platform and can be overridden in tests with `debugDefaultTargetPlatformOverride`.

| Getter | `true` for |
| --- | --- |
| `isWeb`, `isWasm` | web / WebAssembly |
| `isAndroid`, `isIOS`, `isMacOS`, `isWindows`, `isLinux`, `isFuchsia` | that platform (never on web) |
| `isMobile` | Android or iOS |
| `isDesktop` | Windows, Linux or macOS |
| `isCupertino` | iOS or macOS |
| `isMaterial` | Android, Fuchsia, Windows or Linux, or web |

```dart
if (PlayxPlatform.isMobile) { /* ... */ }
```

## WebUtils

Helpers for browser behavior. On the web they use the DOM; on every other platform the same calls compile and are **safe no-ops**, so you don't need `kIsWeb` guards.

| Function | On web | Elsewhere |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `updateUrl(Uri)` | Replaces the URL in the address bar without navigating | no-op |
| `updateQueryParameters(Map<String, String>)` | Replaces the query parameters of the current URL | no-op |
| `setBodyBackgroundColor(String colorHex)` | Sets the `<body>` background | no-op |
| `setAppTitle({required title, primaryColor, webOnly = true})` | Sets the tab title and the app-switcher description | with `webOnly: false`, sets the app-switcher description only |
| `isFullScreen()` | Whether the page is full screen | `false` |
| `enterFullScreen()`, `exitFullScreen()`, `toggleFullScreen()` | Browser full screen | no-op |
| `reloadPage()` | Reloads | no-op |
| `openInNewTab(String url)` | Opens a new tab | no-op |

```dart
WebUtils.setAppTitle(title: 'Playx Core');
WebUtils.updateQueryParameters({'tab': 'settings'});
WebUtils.openInNewTab('https://example.com');
```

Works with both dart2js and WebAssembly builds.

## Colors

```dart
ColorUtils.fromHex(hex: '#336699');                 // opaque
ColorUtils.fromHex(hex: '336699', alpha: 128);      // 50% alpha
ColorUtils.fromRGB(red: 51, green: 102, blue: 153, alpha: 200);
```

For hex strings with the alpha included (`#80336699`) and other helpers, see the [`Color` extensions](extensions.md#color).

## Scroll behavior

`DefaultAppScrollBehavior` lets scrollables be dragged with touch, mouse **and** trackpad, which is handy for web and desktop apps:

```dart
MaterialApp(
  scrollBehavior: DefaultAppScrollBehavior(),
  home: const HomePage(),
);
```

---

<!-- https://playx-flutter.github.io/playx_core/logging/ -->
# Logging

`PlayxLogger` is a small logging facade: static methods that forward to a **default logger**, plus support for any number of **named loggers**. The built-in implementation uses [`talker_logger`](https://pub.dev/packages/talker_logger), and you can plug in any other backend.

## Quick start

`PlayxCore.bootCore` creates a logger named `PLAYX CORE` and makes it the default, so you can log straight away:

```dart
PlayxLogger.i('App started');
PlayxLogger.d('Cart loaded', tag: 'cart');
PlayxLogger.w('Slow response');
PlayxLogger.e('Request failed', error: error, stackTrace: stackTrace);
```

Not using `bootCore`? Create a logger yourself:

```dart
PlayxLogger.initLogger(name: 'APP');
```

If no default logger exists, the static methods do nothing.

## Levels

| Method | Short | Level |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `PlayxLogger.verbose(msg)` | `v` | verbose |
| `PlayxLogger.debug(msg)` | `d` | debug |
| `PlayxLogger.info(msg)` | `i` | info |
| `PlayxLogger.warning(msg)` | `w` | warning |
| `PlayxLogger.error(msg, {error, stackTrace})` | `e` | error |
| `PlayxLogger.critical(msg)` | `c` | critical |
| `PlayxLogger.log(msg)` | | unspecified |

Every method takes a `message` (anything: it is converted with `toString`, and `null` prints as `null`) and an optional `tag`, which is shown in brackets next to the logger name:

```
[APP] [cart] Cart loaded
```

`error` also accepts an `error` and a `stackTrace`, appended below the message.

## Named loggers

```dart
final network = PlayxLogger.initLogger(name: 'NETWORK', setAsDefault: false);
final storage = PlayxLogger.initLogger(name: 'STORAGE', setAsDefault: false);

network.i('GET /users');                       // log with a specific logger
PlayxLogger.getLogger('STORAGE')?.w('Disk almost full');

PlayxLogger.hasLogger('NETWORK');              // true
PlayxLogger.setDefaultLogger(network);         // make it the target of PlayxLogger.i(...)
```

| Member | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `initLogger({name, settings, setAsDefault = true, useColoredFormatter = false})` | Creates a `TalkerPlayxLogger`, registers it under `name` (`PLAYX LOGGER` when omitted), and returns it. It becomes the default when `setAsDefault` is `true`, or when there is no default yet. |
| `getLogger(name)` | The logger registered under `name`, or `null`. |
| `hasLogger(name)` | Whether it exists. |
| `setDefaultLogger(logger)` | Sets any `PlayxBaseLogger` as the default. |

`PlayxCore.logger` returns the `PLAYX CORE` logger created by `bootCore`.

## Message layout

Every message is written as:

```
[time] [LEVEL] [name] [tag] message
```

Each part is optional: the **time** with `printDateTime`, the **level** with `printLevel`, the **logger name** with `printLoggerName` (on by default), and the **tag** when you pass one.

```dart
PlayxLogger.initLogger(
  name: 'APP',
  settings: PlayxLoggerSettings(
    printDateTime: true,
    printLevel: true,
    useColors: false,
    formatter: const DefaultColoredLoggerFormatter(),   // plain lines, no box
  ),
);

PlayxLogger.w('Slow response', tag: 'net');
// [13:45:30.123] [WARNING] [APP] [net] Slow response
```

| Option | Default | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `printLoggerName` | `true` | `[APP] …` |
| `printDateTime` | `false` | `[13:45:30.123] …` |
| `dateTimeFormat` | `PlayxLogDateTimeFormat.time` | `time`: `13:45:30.123`, `dateTime`: `2024-05-15 13:45:30.123`, `iso8601`: `2024-05-15T13:45:30.123` |
| `dateTimeFormatter` | `null` | Your own function (for example with `intl`); overrides `dateTimeFormat`. |
| `printLevel` | `false` | `[INFO] …`: handy when colors are off, because the level is otherwise only shown by color. |

> **Single lines instead of boxes.** The default formatter (`ExtendedLoggerFormatter`) draws a box around each message. `DefaultColoredLoggerFormatter()` prints plain lines, colored only when `useColors` is on. It is what the `PLAYX CORE` logger uses by default.

## Colors and the `flutter:` prefix

Two things can make console output look noisy, and they have different causes.

**1. Escape codes such as `^[[38;5;4m`.** These are ANSI color codes. Terminals render them as colors; some consoles (Xcode, some IDE panels) show them as text. Turn them off:

```dart
PlayxLoggerSettings(useColors: false)
```

Colors are also switched off automatically when they can't be shown, see [Color detection](#color-detection).

**2. The `flutter: ` prefix.** The platform adds it to everything written with `print` or `debugPrint` (`flutter: ` on iOS and macOS, `I/flutter` on Android). The logger can't remove it, but it can use another channel with `target`:

| `target` | Console shows | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `PlayxLogTarget.debugPrint` (default) | `flutter: [APP] hello` | Shown by every console. Safe for long messages. |
| `PlayxLogTarget.stdout` | `[APP] hello` | **No prefix** in a terminal running the app. Some consoles only collect `print` output, such as a mobile device's system log, and may not show it. Falls back to `debugPrint` on web. |
| `PlayxLogTarget.developerLog` | `[APP] hello` under the logger's name, no ANSI codes | Appears in DevTools and IDE debug consoles. **Not** shown in the terminal of `flutter run`. |

These behaviors were checked with `flutter run -d macos`. Try your own console and device: where each channel shows up varies by tool. A custom `output` overrides `target`.

```dart
PlayxLoggerSettings(
  useColors: false,
  target: PlayxLogTarget.stdout,
  formatter: const DefaultColoredLoggerFormatter(),
)
```

### Color detection

With `useColors: true` (the default), colors are still dropped when something says the console can't show them:

| Situation | Colors |
| --- | --- |
| Web, or `target: PlayxLogTarget.developerLog` | off |
| `--dart-define=PLAYX_LOG_COLORS=true` or `false` | forced, whatever else is set (not on web or `developerLog`) |
| `useColors: false` | off |
| `NO_COLOR` environment variable set (non-empty), or `TERM=dumb` | off |
| `target: PlayxLogTarget.stdout` in a terminal that doesn't support ANSI | off |
| Anything else | on |

An app can't see which console shows its `print` output, so on a phone or in an IDE panel colors stay on unless one of the signals above applies.

### Android Studio and IntelliJ

The Run panel doesn't interpret ANSI codes: it prints them as text. Based on the Flutter plugin's source (not tested on every version), there are two ways to get a clean panel:

- **Turn colors off** with a build define. In the run configuration, set *Additional run args* to `--dart-define=PLAYX_LOG_COLORS=false`. No code change is needed, and other developers keep their colors.
- **Use `PlayxLogTarget.developerLog`** for real styling. The IDE shows the logger name as a gray `[name]` prefix, and the `error` and `stackTrace` of `logger.error(...)` in red. The log level is also passed, so DevTools can filter by severity. No ANSI codes are written, and the name is not repeated in the text. The cost: these entries are not printed in the terminal of `flutter run`.

```dart
PlayxLoggerSettings(target: PlayxLogTarget.developerLog)
```

## Configuring the `PLAYX CORE` logger

`bootCore` creates the logger that writes the boot messages (`Booting Preferences...`) and the package's own warnings. Configure it with `loggerSettings`:

```dart
await PlayxCore.bootCore(
  loggerSettings: PlayxLoggerSettings(
    useColors: false,
    printDateTime: true,
    formatter: const DefaultColoredLoggerFormatter(),
  ),
);
```

| Goal | Settings |
| --- | --- |
| No escape codes | `useColors: false` |
| Hide the boot messages, keep warnings and errors | `level: LogLevel.warning` |
| Silence the package completely | `enabled: false` |
| Time on every line | `printDateTime: true` |
| Send the package's logs elsewhere | `output: (message) => ...` |

Without `loggerSettings`, the core logger prints single-line colored messages with `debugPrint` in debug builds, as before. The same logger is the default one for `PlayxLogger.i(...)`, so these settings apply to your own messages too, unless you create another logger and make it the default.

## Settings

```dart
PlayxLogger.initLogger(
  name: 'APP',
  settings: PlayxLoggerSettings(
    enabled: true,                 // log in release builds too
    level: LogLevel.info,          // ignore verbose and debug
    useColors: false,
  ),
);
```

`PlayxLoggerSettings`:

| Option | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `enabled` | `kDebugMode` | Master switch. When `false`, nothing is logged. |
| `printToConsole` | `kDebugMode` | Whether formatted messages are passed to `output` / `target`. When `false` they are discarded (see the note below). |
| `level` | `LogLevel.verbose` | Messages with a lower priority than this are ignored. |
| `useColors` | `true` | ANSI colors. Dropped automatically where they can't be shown: see [Color detection](#color-detection). |
| `colors` | red/yellow/blue/gray per level | Colors per `LogLevel` (`AnsiPen`). |
| `printLoggerName`, `printDateTime`, `dateTimeFormat`, `dateTimeFormatter`, `printLevel` | see [Message layout](#message-layout) | What each message starts with. |
| `formatter` | `ExtendedLoggerFormatter()` | How messages are laid out: `ExtendedLoggerFormatter` (boxed), `ColoredLoggerFormatter`, `DefaultColoredLoggerFormatter` (plain lines), or your own `LoggerFormatter`. `useColoredFormatter: true` in `initLogger` uses the plain one. |
| `lineSymbol` | `─` | The symbol of the separator line. |
| `maxLineWidth` | `140` | Width of the separator line. |
| `target` | `PlayxLogTarget.debugPrint` | The channel used when there is no `output`. See [Colors and the `flutter:` prefix](#colors-and-the-flutter-prefix). |
| `output` | `null` | Where formatted messages go; overrides `target`. |
| `filter` | `null` | A `LoggerFilter` to drop messages. |

> **`printToConsole` and `output`.** With `printToConsole: true` messages go to `output` (or to the `target` when none is given). With `printToConsole: false` nothing is printed, even if you passed an `output`. To send logs somewhere else (a file, a crash reporter), keep `printToConsole: true` and pass `output`.

`LogLevel`, `AnsiPen`, `LoggerFormatter`, `LoggerFilter`, `LoggerOutput`, `LogDetails`, `ExtendedLoggerFormatter`, `ColoredLoggerFormatter` and `TalkerLoggerSettings` are re-exported by `playx_core`, so you don't need to depend on `talker_logger` yourself.

### Sending logs elsewhere

```dart
PlayxLogger.initLogger(
  name: 'APP',
  settings: PlayxLoggerSettings(
    enabled: true,
    printToConsole: true,
    output: (message) => crashReporter.addBreadcrumb(message),
  ),
);
```

### Release builds

`enabled` and `printToConsole` default to `kDebugMode`, so a default logger is **silent in release builds**. Enable it explicitly (as above) if you want logs in production, ideally with a `level` of `warning` or higher and an `output` that goes to your reporting tool.

## Your own logger

Implement `PlayxBaseLogger` to use another backend (for example `package:logger`, Sentry or Crashlytics) and make it the default:

```dart
class SentryLogger extends PlayxBaseLogger {
  const SentryLogger() : super(name: 'SENTRY');

  @override
  void debug(message, {String? tag}) => Sentry.addBreadcrumb(Breadcrumb(message: '$message'));

  @override
  void info(message, {String? tag}) => Sentry.addBreadcrumb(Breadcrumb(message: '$message'));

  @override
  void warning(message, {String? tag}) => Sentry.captureMessage('$message', level: SentryLevel.warning);

  @override
  void error(message, {Object? error, StackTrace? stackTrace, String? tag}) =>
      Sentry.captureException(error ?? message, stackTrace: stackTrace);

  @override
  void critical(message, {String? tag}) => Sentry.captureMessage('$message', level: SentryLevel.fatal);

  @override
  void verbose(message, {String? tag}) {}

  @override
  void log(message, {String? tag}) {}
}

PlayxLogger.setDefaultLogger(const SentryLogger());
```

You only implement the seven level methods: the short aliases (`d`, `i`, `w`, `e`, `c`, `v`, `l`) are provided by the base class.

## What `playx_core` logs

The package logs through the `PLAYX CORE` logger, for example:

- startup steps (`Booting Preferences...`), configurable with [`bootCore(loggerSettings:)`](#configuring-the-playx-core-logger);
- skipped env files and reads before `PlayxEnv.load`;
- secure storage fallbacks and failures (`auto` choosing another backend, an unreadable key, a lost key);
- errors in `MapUtils` helpers when `printError` is set.

Messages never include secret values. In release builds nothing is printed unless you enabled the logger.

# Testing

How to test your own code that uses `playx_core`, and how to run this package's tests.

- [A typical test setup](#a-typical-test-setup)
- [Preferences](#preferences)
- [Secure preferences](#secure-preferences)
- [Environment configuration](#environment-configuration)
- [Platform behavior](#platform-behavior)
- [Logging](#logging)
- [Web tests](#web-tests)
- [Testing the `secure_env` command](#testing-the-secure_env-command)
- [Running this package's tests](#running-this-packages-tests)

## A typical test setup

Boot the core with in-memory storage and no isolates, and dispose it after each test:

```dart
import 'package:flutter_test/flutter_test.dart';
import 'package:playx_core/playx_core.dart';
import 'package:shared_preferences_platform_interface/in_memory_shared_preferences_async.dart';
import 'package:shared_preferences_platform_interface/shared_preferences_async_platform_interface.dart';

void main() {
  TestWidgetsFlutterBinding.ensureInitialized();

  setUp(() async {
    PlayxPrefs.setMockInitialValues({});
    SharedPreferencesAsyncPlatform.instance = InMemorySharedPreferencesAsync.empty();

    await PlayxCore.bootCore(
      securePrefsSettings: const PlayxSecurePrefsSettings(
        storageType: PlayxSecureStorageType.memory,
        clearOnReinstall: false,
      ),
      workerManagerSettings: const WorkManagerSettings(initWorkerManager: false),
    );
  });

  tearDown(PlayxCore.dispose);

  test('stores the counter', () async {
    await PlayxPrefs.setInt('counter', 3);
    expect(PlayxPrefs.getInt('counter'), 3);
  });
}
```

Add `shared_preferences_platform_interface` as a `dev_dependency` to use the in-memory async store.

## Preferences

| Store | How to prepare it in tests |
| --- | --- |
| `PlayxPrefs` | `PlayxPrefs.setMockInitialValues({...})`, then `await PlayxPrefs.create()` |
| `PlayxAsyncPrefs`, `PlayxPrefsWithCache` | `SharedPreferencesAsyncPlatform.instance = InMemorySharedPreferencesAsync.empty()` (or `.withData({...})`), then `create()` |

```dart
PlayxPrefs.setMockInitialValues({'name': 'Jane'});
await PlayxPrefs.create();
expect(PlayxPrefs.getString('name'), 'Jane');
```

Reset between tests with `PlayxPrefs.clear()` / `dispose()`, or `PlayxCore.dispose()`.

## Secure preferences

Use the `memory` backend: no plugins, no platform channels.

```dart
await PlayxSecurePrefs.create(
  securePrefsSettings: const PlayxSecurePrefsSettings(
    storageType: PlayxSecureStorageType.memory,
    clearOnReinstall: false,
  ),
);
```

`clearOnReinstall: false` avoids touching `SharedPreferences` during setup. Call `await PlayxSecurePrefs.dispose()` afterwards.

To test **your fallback handling** (what happens when secure storage fails), fake the plugins' platform interfaces. This package's own tests do it, see [`test/prefs/secure_prefs_test.dart`](https://github.com/playx-flutter/playx_core/blob/main/test/prefs/secure_prefs_test.dart):

```dart
// Fakes for simple_secure_storage and flutter_secure_storage:
SimpleSecureStoragePlatform.instance = FakeSimpleSecureStorage()..failInitialize = true;
FlutterSecureStoragePlatform.instance = FakeFlutterSecureStorage();

await PlayxSecurePrefs.create(
  securePrefsSettings: const PlayxSecurePrefsSettings(storageType: PlayxSecureStorageType.auto),
);
expect(PlayxSecurePrefs.storageType, PlayxSecureStorageType.flutterSecureStorage);
```

## Environment configuration

Three ways, from simplest to most realistic:

**1. Set the values directly.**

```dart
PlayxEnv.setMockValues({'API_URL': 'http://localhost', 'RETRIES': '3'});
// ...
await PlayxEnv.dispose();
```

**2. Load `.env` text.**

```dart
PlayxEnv.loadFromString(
  'API_URL=http://localhost\nRETRIES=3',
  mergeWith: {'RETRIES': '5'},
  usePlayxDefines: false,   // ignore --dart-define values of the test run
);
```

**3. Load the real asset files.** `PlayxEnv.load` reads Flutter assets. In unit tests, serve them from memory:

```dart
void mockAssets(Map<String, String> files) {
  TestDefaultBinaryMessengerBinding.instance.defaultBinaryMessenger
      .setMockMessageHandler('flutter/assets', (message) async {
    final key = utf8.decode(message!.buffer.asUint8List());
    final content = files[Uri.decodeFull(key)];
    if (content == null) return null;                          // missing file
    return ByteData.sublistView(Uint8List.fromList(utf8.encode(content)));
  });
}

setUp(() => mockAssets({
      '.env': 'API_URL=https://api.example.com',
      '.env.prod': 'API_URL=https://api.prod.example.com',
    }));

test('prod overrides the base', () async {
  await PlayxEnv.load(const PlayxEnvSettings(environment: 'prod'));
  expect(PlayxEnv.getString('API_URL'), 'https://api.prod.example.com');
});
```

Or load the files your app actually ships, as the [example app's tests](https://github.com/playx-flutter/playx_core/blob/main/example/test/env_test.dart) do (widget tests can read real assets).

**Build flags.** Tests can run with defines and flavors to cover those code paths:

```sh
flutter test --dart-define=PLAYX_ENV=prod
flutter test --dart-define=PLAYX_DEFINES="DEBUG=true"
flutter test --flavor staging
```

Because `usePlayxDefines` is on by default, a `PLAYX_DEFINES` value passed to the test run also applies to tests that don't expect it. Pass `usePlayxDefines: false` in such tests.

**Secure env.** Build `PlayxSecureEnvData` in the test with the same codec the command uses, or point a test at the generated file of your app:

```dart
import 'generated/playx_secure_env.g.dart';

await PlayxEnv.load(const PlayxEnvSettings(secureEnv: playxSecureEnv));
expect(PlayxEnv.isSecure('STRIPE_KEY'), isTrue);
```

## Platform behavior

**Platform checks** (`PlayxPlatform`) follow Flutter's override:

```dart
debugDefaultTargetPlatformOverride = TargetPlatform.android;
addTearDown(() => debugDefaultTargetPlatformOverride = null);

expect(PlayxPlatform.isAndroid, isTrue);
```

**System UI, orientation and clipboard** go through the `SystemChannels.platform` channel. Mock it to assert what is sent:

```dart
final calls = <MethodCall>[];
TestDefaultBinaryMessengerBinding.instance.defaultBinaryMessenger
    .setMockMethodCallHandler(SystemChannels.platform, (call) async {
  calls.add(call);
  return null;
});

setOrientation(isPortrait: false);

expect(calls.single.method, 'SystemChrome.setPreferredOrientations');
expect(calls.single.arguments, ['DeviceOrientation.landscapeLeft']);
```

`WebUtils` is a no-op outside the browser, so it needs no setup in VM tests.

## Logging

Capture output by giving the logger an `output`:

```dart
final lines = <String>[];
final logger = TalkerPlayxLogger(
  settings: PlayxLoggerSettings(enabled: true, printToConsole: true, useColors: false, output: lines.add),
  name: 'TEST',
);
logger.info('hello');
expect(lines.join(), contains('hello'));
```

`PlayxLogger.setDefaultLogger(...)` with a recording `PlayxBaseLogger` lets you assert on what the package logs. See [Logging](logging.md#your-own-logger).

## Web tests

Code that behaves differently on the web (`WebUtils`, the WebCrypto key store, secure prefs on web) is tested in a browser:

```dart
@TestOn('browser')
library;
```

```sh
flutter test --platform chrome test/utils/web_utils_web_test.dart
```

## Testing the `secure_env` command

The command is a function you can call from tests, with temporary directories and captured output:

```dart
import 'package:playx_core/secure_env_cli.dart';

final out = StringBuffer();
final code = await runSecureEnvCli(
  ['--env', 'prod'],
  environment: {'PLAYX_ENV': 'prod'},   // instead of the process environment
  workingDirectory: tempDir.path,
  stdoutSink: out,
  stderrSink: StringBuffer(),
  executableName: 'playx_core:secure_env',
);
expect(code, 0);
```

See [`test/env/secure_env_cli_test.dart`](https://github.com/playx-flutter/playx_core/blob/main/test/env/secure_env_cli_test.dart) for many examples, including decrypting the generated file.

## Running this package's tests

```sh
flutter test                                              # VM tests
flutter test --coverage                                   # writes coverage/lcov.info
flutter test --platform chrome test/prefs/secure_prefs_web_test.dart \
  test/env/secure_env_web_test.dart test/utils/web_utils_web_test.dart   # browser tests
```

Some tests only run when the matching build flag is passed, and are skipped otherwise:

```sh
flutter test test/env --dart-define=PLAYX_ENV=prod
flutter test test/env --flavor staging
flutter test test/env '--dart-define=PLAYX_DEFINES=PD_DEBUG=true;PD_NAME=define'
```

The `secure_env` define tests need `PLAYX_ENV_KEY` and `PLAYX_SECURE_DEFINES`; see the comments in [`test/env/secure_env_test.dart`](https://github.com/playx-flutter/playx_core/blob/main/test/env/secure_env_test.dart) for how to create them with the command.

<!-- https://playx-flutter.github.io/playx_core/migration-2.0/ -->
# Migrating from 1.x to 2.0

2.0 raises the minimum SDK and changes a few APIs, mostly in `PlayxEnv` and `PlayxSecurePrefs`. Most apps need only a handful of edits. Work through the checklist in order, then run `flutter analyze`: nearly every change below is caught at compile time.

- [Checklist](#checklist)
- [1. Upgrade Dart and Flutter](#1-upgrade-dart-and-flutter)
- [2. PlayxEnv](#2-playxenv)
- [3. Secure preferences settings](#3-secure-preferences-settings)
- [4. Secure preferences on web](#4-secure-preferences-on-web)
- [5. Smaller behavior changes](#5-smaller-behavior-changes)
- [6. Dependencies](#6-dependencies)
- [What did not change](#what-did-not-change)
- [New in 2.0](#new-in-20)

## Checklist

| | Change | Affects you if… |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ☐ | Dart ≥ 3.12 and Flutter ≥ 3.44 | always |
| ☐ | `PlayxEnv` getters are synchronous | you call `PlayxEnv.get*` / `maybeGet*` |
| ☐ | `PlayxEnv.load` takes a `PlayxEnvSettings` | you call `PlayxEnv.load(...)` yourself |
| ☐ | `PlayxEnv.instance` is removed | you read `PlayxEnv.instance` or `dotenv` |
| ☐ | Bool parsing is stricter | you read bools from env or secure prefs |
| ☐ | `PlayxSecurePrefsSettings` options are grouped | you customize secure storage options |
| ☐ | `AndroidOptions(encryptedSharedPreferences: …)` is gone | you set it |
| ☐ | Secure storage on web uses WebCrypto | you target web |
| ☐ | `WebUtils.setAppTitle` takes named arguments | you call it |
| ☐ | `context.form` returns `null` outside a `Form` | you use it |
| ☐ | Dependency versions | your app pins `flutter_secure_storage`, `flutter_dotenv` or `get_it` |

## 1. Upgrade Dart and Flutter

| | 1.x | 2.0 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Dart | 3.5 | **3.12** |
| Flutter | 3.24 | **3.44** |

```yaml
environment:
  sdk: '>=3.12.0 <4.0.0'
  flutter: '>=3.44.0'
```

The new floor comes from `simple_secure_storage` (see [Secure preferences](secure-prefs.md)). If you can't upgrade yet, stay on 1.x.

## 2. PlayxEnv

`PlayxEnv` was rewritten around synchronous reads and a settings object. Details: [Environment configuration](env.md).

### Getters are synchronous

Values are in memory after `load`, so there is nothing to await.

```dart
// 1.x
final url = await PlayxEnv.getString('API_URL');
final retries = await PlayxEnv.getInt('RETRIES', fallback: 3);

// 2.0
final url = PlayxEnv.getString('API_URL');
final retries = PlayxEnv.getInt('RETRIES', fallback: 3);
```

A leftover `await` still compiles (and `flutter analyze` flags it with `await_only_futures`), but code that treated the result as a `Future` (`.then(...)`, `Future<String>` variables) no longer compiles. Search for `PlayxEnv.` in your project.

### `load` takes a `PlayxEnvSettings`

```dart
// 1.x
await PlayxEnv.load(fileName: '.env.dev', mergeWith: {'A': '1'}, isOptional: false);

// 2.0
await PlayxEnv.load(
  const PlayxEnvSettings(fileName: '.env.dev', mergeWith: {'A': '1'}, isOptional: false),
);
```

`PlayxEnvSettings` keeps its four original options (`fileName`, `parser`, `mergeWith`, `isOptional`), so the `envSettings:` argument of `bootCore` needs no change.

### `PlayxEnv.instance` is removed

`PlayxEnv` no longer fills `flutter_dotenv`'s global `dotenv`.

| 1.x | 2.0 |
| --- | --- |
| `PlayxEnv.instance.env` / `dotenv.env` | `PlayxEnv.all` (secure values excluded) |
| `PlayxEnv.instance.isInitialized` | `PlayxEnv.isLoaded` |
| `PlayxEnv.instance.isEveryDefined([...])` | `requiredKeys` in the settings, or `PlayxEnv.values.missingKeys([...]).isEmpty` |
| `dotenv.get('KEY')` | `PlayxEnv.getString('KEY')` |

### Stricter bool parsing

| Value | 1.x `getBool` | 2.0 `getBool` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `true`, `TRUE`, `1` | `true` | `true` |
| `false`, `0` | `false` | `false` |
| `yes`, `maybe`, garbage | `false` | the **fallback** (`maybeGetBool` gives `null`) |

If you relied on "anything else is false", pass an explicit `fallback: false` (the default), or normalize your values.

`getInt` and `getDouble` also became more lenient: `"3.9"` reads as `3` for ints and `3` as `3.0` for doubles.

### Missing files and keys

Missing env files are now **logged and skipped** (as before for optional files), and you can add `requiredKeys` to fail at startup with a `PlayxEnvException` listing everything that is missing.

## 3. Secure preferences settings

The native `flutter_secure_storage` options moved into one object, and `webOptions` was removed (see [web](#4-secure-preferences-on-web)).

```dart
// 1.x
const PlayxSecurePrefsSettings(
  iosOptions: IOSOptions(accessibility: KeychainAccessibility.unlocked),
  androidOptions: AndroidOptions(encryptedSharedPreferences: true),
);

// 2.0
const PlayxSecurePrefsSettings(
  flutterSecureStorageOptions: PlayxFlutterSecureStorageOptions(
    iosOptions: IOSOptions(accessibility: KeychainAccessibility.unlocked),
    androidOptions: AndroidOptions(),
  ),
);
```

Moved options: `iosOptions`, `androidOptions`, `linuxOptions`, `windowsOptions`, `macOsOptions`. `clearOnReinstall` and `createSecurePrefs` are unchanged.

### `encryptedSharedPreferences` is gone

`flutter_secure_storage` 11 removed it and migrates existing Android data automatically on first access. Delete the argument (or the whole `AndroidOptions`).

### Staying on the same storage

The default is still `flutter_secure_storage`, so nothing changes about **where** your data lives. To move to the new backends, follow [Switching an existing app](secure-prefs.md#switching-an-existing-app-from-flutter_secure_storage).

## 4. Secure preferences on web

On web, `PlayxSecurePrefs` now encrypts with a **non-extractable WebCrypto key** kept in IndexedDB for every storage type except `memory`, instead of `flutter_secure_storage`'s web implementation (which kept its key in `localStorage`).

- Existing values are **migrated automatically** on the first start.
- Remove `webOptions` and any wrap-key configuration: there is nothing to configure now.
- Values written directly to `PlayxSecurePrefs.securePrefs` on web are no longer where playx reads and writes. Use the `PlayxSecurePrefs` API instead.

Details: [Secure preferences, Web](secure-prefs.md#web).

## 5. Smaller behavior changes

| Area | 1.x | 2.0 | Action |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `WebUtils.setAppTitle` | positional on web (`setAppTitle('x')`), named on other platforms | named everywhere: `setAppTitle(title: 'x')` | Use the named form. The two forms could not compile on both platforms before. |
| `WebUtils` on WebAssembly | silently the no-op version | the real web version | none |
| `context.form` | threw outside a `Form` | returns `null` | none (a fix) |
| `asListInt` / `asListIntOr` | rejected `[1, '2', 3.0]` | convert like `asListIntOrNull`: `[1, 2, 3]` | none (a fix) |
| `PlayxSecurePrefs.maybeGetInt` / `Double` / `Bool` | `int.parse`, `double.parse`, `== 'true'` or `'1'` | `safe_convert` helpers | See [stricter bool parsing](#stricter-bool-parsing) |
| `PlayxAsyncPrefs.maybeGet*` | async errors escaped | errors return `null` as documented | none (a fix) |
| `clearOnReinstall` | required `PlayxPrefs` to be created | reads `SharedPreferences` itself, with the same flag | none |

## 6. Dependencies

| Package | 1.x | 2.0 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `flutter_secure_storage` | `^10` | `^11.2` |
| `simple_secure_storage` | not used | `^0.4.3` |
| `flutter_dotenv` | `^6.0` | `^6.0.1` |
| `pointycastle` | not used | `>=3.9.1 <5.0.0` |
| `get_it` | `^9.2` | `>=8.0.0 <10.0.0` |
| `shared_preferences` | `^2.5.5` | `>=2.3.0 <3.0.0` |
| `equatable` | `^2.0.8` | `>=2.0.7 <4.0.0` |

If `flutter pub get` reports a version conflict, check that your app doesn't pin `flutter_secure_storage` below 11. New plugins mean new native code: run a full rebuild after upgrading (`flutter clean`, and `pod install` on iOS and macOS).

## What did not change

- `PlayxCore.bootCore`, `getIt`, `PlayxCore.dispose`.
- The `PlayxPrefs`, `PlayxAsyncPrefs` and `PlayxPrefsWithCache` APIs (new methods were added).
- The `PlayxSecurePrefs` API and its default backend.
- The `PlayxLogger` API.
- All `safe_convert` and `safe_json_convert` functions (new optional parameters only).

## New in 2.0

Not required for the upgrade, but worth a look:

- **More secure storage backends and a resilient `auto` mode:** [Secure preferences](secure-prefs.md).
- **Hiding key names** with `encryptKeys`: [Secure preferences](secure-prefs.md#hiding-key-names-encryptkeys).
- **Environments, flavors, `--dart-define` and typed getters:** [Environment configuration](env.md).
- **Encrypted secrets** generated by a command: [Secure env](secure-env.md).
- **Maps, lists and objects** in every preference store: [Preferences](preferences.md#maps-lists-and-objects).
- **Padding, border and radius helpers** and more: [Extensions](extensions.md).
- A full list in the [changelog](https://pub.dev/packages/playx_core/changelog).
